name: AkaCE
full_title: Akan Cinematic Emotions: A Multimodal Multi-party Dataset for Emotion Recognition in Movie Dialogues
license_note: LICENSE.txt (AkaCE Dataset License Agreement): non-commercial academic research and educational purposes only; redistribution, including of derived data, is forbidden; citing the paper is required. The README says non-commercial research only. GitHub shows NOASSERTION.
labels_discrete_note: The label table also has two classes with one row each, Frustration and Confusion (9 classes in the table; the paper lists 7). The table calls the class Joy, the paper Happy. 24 rows share a segment with a different emotion.
label_basis_note: Annotators saw the video as well as hearing the audio; the voice alone was not rated.
source_rights_note: Audio and video are cut from 21 Akan movies; the README (non-commercial research only) says nothing about the rights in the films. Needs a rights check (needs-confirmation list); license_class keeps the stated license.
notes: Sasu et al. (Findings of ACL 2025). 385 dialogues, 6,162 utterances, 308 speakers (gender-balanced). 16 kHz audio. Also called ACE. Table splits are 4,498/935/729 (paper 3,888/816/834); the GitHub copy has another split (split1) used by the official code. Audio segments carry a 1.5 s margin after the annotation end and some times are wrong, so 332 segments exceed 30 s (longest 498.5 s). Movie me_sofo_anyim_me_yere (33 rows) has table times in a shifted unit (00m:01s:12ms) and its segments do not match the utterances. Hours: the paper's 87,441 s (24.3 h, with 227.1 s per dialogue) is the dialogue total and not the sum of utterances; the utterance segments used by the recipe total 15.34 h. Google Drive download needs no login; the audio folder holds several versions.

name: AlbEmo
full_title: AlbEmo: an emotional speech corpus for Albanian
license_note: Zenodo record 21638085 (AlbEmo v1.0, 2026-07-28): CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo API re-read 2026-10-26; the archive also has a LICENSE file); checked by the maintainer.
label_basis_note: Label = the intended emotion (folder names gezim, zemerim, frike, habi, neveri, trishtim, neutral). 4 native listeners rated every clip three times in a blind forced-choice test (evaluations/ holds 30 per-rater files, aggregated results and a confusion matrix). The recipe does not use the ratings.
notes: AlbEmo (University of Tirana), first emotional speech corpus for Albanian; Zenodo 21638085, 92 MB. Ten native Albanian speakers (5 female, 5 male; aged 18 to over 55) recorded six semantically neutral sentences in seven styles (Ekman's six emotions and neutral): 420 recordings, 48 kHz 16-bit mono, 22.1 min (0.3679 h), clips 1.2-10.1 s. Recorded alone in a quiet office with a USB cardioid microphone and a purpose-built offline browser tool, with browser-side processing disabled. Folder names are Albanian emotion words. Listening test: 4 evaluators, 1,260 judgements; in the review's recount 918 judgements are correct; the majority differs from the intention for 63 clips and no evaluator got 31 clips right (disgust 15). Evaluation file inconsistencies (memo only): five files audit_ev01_sp04.csv to sp08.csv have rater ev02 inside, so by the column sp05-sp08 (168 clips) would have two raters, and some files have extra note columns. The scripts/, tools/ and README mentioned in the description are not in the downloaded archive (the record lists them).

name: ANAD
full_title: Arabic Natural Audio Dataset
language_note: Arabic (phone-in callers on talk shows). Dialect not checked
license_note: Kaggle license field: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
labels_discrete_note: Labels are constant per video (call): V1, V3, V8 = happy; V2, V6 = surprised; V4, V5, V7 = angry. The release has 1,334 clips with both label and wav (the table has 1,383 rows): angry 723, happy 469, surprised 142. The 566 clips used by the recipe are angry 404, happy 154, surprise 8, almost all from two videos, V7 (angry 376) and V8 (happy 149).
label_basis_note: Eight live phone calls on Arabic talk shows. 18 listeners chose for each video whether they perceived happy, angry or surprised (the per-video label is copied to every 1-second chunk). Whether raters also watched the video is not stated ("listen to each video").
notes: Samira Klaylat (Kaggle uploader) et al. Eight live calls from Arabic talk shows were downloaded, split at speaker turns, and 18 listeners chose among happy, angry and surprised. Silence, laughter and noise were removed and the rest automatically cut into 1-second units: 1,384 clips. A CSV of 950-dimensional acoustic features is included. Kaggle version v11 (2017-12-01). Paper: Klaylat, Osman, Hamandi, Zantout, Emotion recognition in Arabic speech, Analog Integrated Circuits and Signal Processing 96(2), 337-351 (2018) (bibliography checked via Crossref; full text not read). No speaker IDs. Two groups of 386 and 382 clips appear with near-identical sound under different videos and labels (the maintainer listened to 6 and confirmed). The recipe (egs3/anad/cls, on hold) uses the 566 clips without these 768; split train 396 / valid 56 / test 114 (after the length filter 349 / 33 / 114), max_epochs 273. No health check after the exclusion. Two short groups (0.29 s and 0.31 s) were not excluded.

name: ASED
license_note: The repository (wgwangang/ASED_V1) has no LICENSE file (GitHub shows none) and the README states no terms of use or citation request (re-read 2026-10-26). Terms for research use, redistribution and commercial use are unknown. The maintainer will ask the authors (Northwest University); not yet contacted. Until then the data is used locally only.
label_basis_note: Label = the emotion the participant was asked to speak (folder / file-name code). Eight judges reviewed every recording; only recordings accepted by at least five (emotion-specific sentences: accepted as expressing the emotion; common sentences: five or more chose the same emotion) are in the release. The judges' individual answers are not distributed.
notes: Amharic Speech Emotional Dataset v1 (ASED), Northwest University, created 2021-02-12. 65 participants (25 female, 40 male) recorded 70 sentences each at a time and place of their choice (semi-supervised): 25 emotion-specific sentences twice (5 per emotion) and 2 common sentences twice in each of 5 emotions. 2,474 wav accepted by the judges (anger 469-522 per class), 2.0-3.9 s in 9 distinct lengths (42% exactly 3.0 s), 2.1058 h. Folders 01Neutral to 05Angry; file name xn-yy-aa-gg-bb (emotion code, sentence 01-07, repetition, gender code, speaker). Sentences 03-07 are the emotion-specific ones (all-or-nothing per speaker: 37 speakers have all 50, 28 have none, per the review). Duplicates: 53 groups (106 files) of identical sound with no label conflicts: 50 are repetitions 1 and 2 of the same speaker, sentence and emotion, 2 are between speakers 23 and 25 and 1 is another sentence of speaker 57 (from the review).

name: ASVP-ESD
full_title: Audio, Speech and Vision Processing Lab Emotional Sound Database (ASVP-ESD)
license_note: Zenodo record 4782712 (2021-05-24): CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo API re-read 2026-10-26; checked by the maintainer). CC BY 4.0 covers the compilation; the rights in the original recordings of films, TV and web videos are separate (see source_rights).
label_basis_note: Label = the class with the most votes among annotators who listened to each clip and chose a label by personal feeling (5 annotators for the first 52 folders, 3 other annotators for the later ones). Individual votes are not distributed. The folder name and file name carry the emotion code. The recipe uses 7 of the 12 emotions.
source_rights_note: The Zenodo record says the audio comes from movies, TV shows, YouTube channels and emotion-sound websites and licenses the compilation under CC BY 4.0; it names no sources and says nothing about the rights of the original recordings. The project members will decide whether to use it. Needs a rights check (needs-confirmation list); license_class keeps the stated license.
notes: Audio, Speech and Vision Processing Lab Emotional Sound database (South China University of Technology), Zenodo 4782712, 1.26 GB. 7,812 audio files in 78 folders (odd = female, even = male; some folders hold dialogue or several people) plus 1,204 files in two folders of babies' voices (acteur_50, acteur_150); speech and non-speech sounds in 12 emotions (boredom, neutral, happiness, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, disgust, excitement, pleasure, pain, disappointment) at two intensities (normal, high); 16 kHz mono wav, 0.5-20 s, about 10 h 51 min. Labelled by listeners with a vote (5 annotators for the first 52 folders, 3 others for later ones). The recipe's Bonus clips: 25 (all happy; their Whisper transcripts are repetitions or nonsense). Same-sound groups: 22 (14 with the same emotion, one kept by exclude_duplicates; 8 with different emotions, 16 clips, always left out by the maintainer's decision) (from the review). File-name fields vary between 8 and 12 and hold values (language, source, intensity) that the description does not explain.

notes: Speech sentiment data on Kaggle. 250 TRAIN clips (labels in `TRAIN.csv`), 110 TEST clips (no labels), 360 mel-spectrogram PNG images. wav 44.1 kHz stereo (240 PCM_16, 120 64-bit float), 1.698-3.944 s (TRAIN total 0.184 h). No duplicates. The following comes only from light checks (Whisper large-v3 transcripts, F0 distribution, the maintainer's listening), not human verification: English sentences (67 sentences used in 145 clips, every recording of a sentence has the same label); probably a single speaker (F0 5th-95th percentile 128-148 Hz). No information on speakers, gender, sentences, origin, authors or labelling procedure. Whether the voice was acted to match the sentence polarity was not checked.

Official split: 86 training and 20 test participants (as described by HiCMAE).

full_title: BanglaMood: A Rich Audio Dataset for Eight Emotion Recognition in Bangla Speech
license_note: Mendeley Data record: CC BY 4.0 (checked by the maintainer, 2026-10-28). The license field covers the compilers' work; see source_rights.
source_rights_note: Clips cut from YouTube videos. The Mendeley record (CC BY 4.0) says nothing about the rights in the videos, and there is no paper; the Mendeley CC BY 4.0 text itself notes that further permission may be required for content belonging to a third party. The method says the videos were chosen at random from publicly available YouTube videos (short stories, vlogs). Needs a rights check (needs-confirmation list); license_class keeps the stated license.
notes: Labelling looked at the video (faces, scene) as well as the audio (description). The description says all files are 5 seconds, but they measure 0.52-7.57 s. One pair with identical SHA-256 and conflicting labels (Disappointment/Male/0737 and Neutral/Male/0704) is dropped entirely, leaving 3,218 clips. No paper found. No speaker or source-video information. Source: Patwary, Hossain, Hossain, Rahman, 'BanglaMood: A Rich Audio Dataset for Eight Emotion Recognition in Bangla Speech', Mendeley Data V3, doi 10.17632/9cc8k5v7w4.3 (version 3 published 2025-07-02; version 1 2025-06-24). The record's articles field is empty. Classes: angry, neutral, fear, disappointed, sad, surprise, happy, excited. The description says all clips are 5 seconds; measured 0.52-7.57 s. Always dropped: Disappointment/Male/0737 and Neutral/Male/0704 (identical bytes, different labels).

name: BanglaSER
full_title: BanglaSER: A speech emotion recognition dataset for the Bangla language
license_note: Mendeley Data version 5 (2022-03-14): CC BY 4.0 (Mendeley API re-read 2026-10-26; checked by the maintainer).
notes: BanglaSER (Data in Brief 2022, PMC8980634); Mendeley Data t9h6p943xy, version 5. 34 nonprofessional actors (17 male, 17 female, 19-47 years) recorded 3 scripted statements x 3 repetitions in 4 emotions (angry, happy, sad, surprise) and neutral from 27 speakers: 1,467 wav (3 to 4 s cut with Audacity; 44.1 and 48 kHz, mono and stereo mixed), 1.374 h measured (the paper says about 1 h 29 min and 44.1 kHz). File name mode-statement type-emotion-intensity-statement-repetition-actor (odd actor = male). Same-sound groups: 8, all with the same label (7 are repetitions of the same speaker, statement and emotion and one is surprise by actors 16 and 19; 2 groups are byte-identical, the others identical after decoding, per the review). File-name faults: three surprise files of actor 15 carry mode 01, and actor 19's folder has one file named like an actor 3 file with different audio. Mendeley versions 1-4 differ from version 5 (not compared).

name: BanSpEmo
full_title: BanSpEmo: A Bangla Emotional Speech Recognition Dataset
license_note: Mendeley Data (BANSpEmo, version 1 holds the audio): CC BY 4.0 (Mendeley API re-read 2026-10-26; checked by the maintainer). Version 2 (2023-05-30) holds only an MFCC table.
notes: BANSpEmo (Green University of Bangladesh), arXiv 2312.14020, Mendeley Data rdwn4bs5ky. 22 unprofessional student speakers (11 male, 11 female) recorded two sets of six Bangla sentences in six emotions: set 1 by 18 speakers (10 male, 8 female) and set 2 by 4 speakers (1 male, 3 female), one repetition each: 792 recordings, 3-12 s, 1.3867 h measured (the paper says 1 h 23 min 12 s), 44.1 and 48 kHz stereo. The paper's '12 sentences' means two sets of six, not twelve per speaker. No neutral class.

name: BARI-EmoSpeech
full_title: BARI-EmoSpeech: A Dialect-Specific Speech Emotion Recognition Dataset for Barishal Bangla
license_note: Mendeley Data license field: CC BY 4.0.
label_basis_note: The distributor says the utterances are spontaneous and were collected with culturally relevant prompts (e.g. festival memories for happiness). Labels come from dual annotation (Fleiss' kappa = 0.82). However, listening found no voice difference between emotions; emotions appear to be separated by sentence content (excluded in the review of 2026-10-23).
notes: Mendeley Data hpfv67fgb8 version 1 (2025-10-10, Daffodil International University). Barishal-dialect Bengali, 5 emotions (Affection, Happiness, Jealousy, Normal, Sadness). The description promises 16 kHz WAV, a train/val split and a CSV (speaker, duration), but the release is 2,312 m4a files (AAC etc.) in emotion folders with no split and no CSV. "Five native Barishal speakers (aged 22-45, gender-balanced) collected samples" can mean they spoke or that they collected. On listening, all clips sound like the same (child-like) female voice, and a speaker model (ESPnet-SPK SKA-TDNN trained on VoxCeleb; EER 24% on the reference SUBESCO) puts 2,204 of 2,303 clips (96%) in one cluster. The 99 outliers (70 of them normal) were not listened to. No voice difference between emotions could be heard, and transcripts show the sentence content itself expresses the emotion (e.g. sadness: "the happy days are over"; affection: "don't look at your phone while eating"). Therefore not used. The speaker and content checks were provisional and of low reliability (2026-10-23). Whisper language ID also gives mostly bn (94% of the 682 clips with confidence >= 0.9).

name: BASER
full_title: Bangla Adolescent Speech Emotion Recognition
license_note: Kaggle license field: Apache 2.0 (checked by the maintainer on 2026-10-23). Includes minors aged 12-19 with no statement of consent; by the maintainer's decision this is not treated as a problem.
label_basis_note: Acted by non-professional actors aged 12-19. Labels are the emotions acted (file names). No listening check is described.
notes: Md Jabed Hossain. 12 non-professional adolescent actors aged 12-19. The description does not list the emotions. Kaggle `jabedcse/baser-dataset` (version 1, 2023-12-16, author Md Jabed Hossain). Acted Bengali speech. The description says 12 non-professional actors aged 12-19 (6 male, 6 female), but the release has 10 speakers (5 female: CHAITY, IRA, MAHI, TABASSUM, Tahsin; 5 male: HASAN, MIFTA, MAHMUD, RIAD, JUHAYER); the reason is unknown (as of 2026-10-23). Each speaker: 5 sentences x 5 emotions (angry, fear, happy, neutral, sad) x 3 takes = 75 clips; 750 in total (150 per emotion), 48 kHz mono 16-bit, 1.714-5.013 s, 0.6059 h. No sentence texts (transcripts). The Kaggle page cites no paper. 58 of the 750 clips duplicate the same sound (speaker RIAD has byte-identical takes in all 25 groups (50 redundant), plus 7 clips in 6 other groups, plus 1 clip with a different byte stream but the same waveform); confirmed by the maintainer's listening. The recipe keeps the lowest take of each group and uses 692 clips.

name: BERSt
full_title: B(asic) E(motion) R(andom phrase) S(hou)t(s)
language_note: English (regional accents from the UK, Canada, US and Australia, and non-native speakers of French, Russian, Hindi, etc.)
license_note: Hugging Face card: CC BY 4.0.
label_basis_note: 98 professional actors performed phrases at three levels: speaking, raising the voice and shouting. Labels are the emotions given to the actors; the card states they were not validated through perception.
notes: Rosie Lab (Simon Fraser University). Computer Speech & Language 2025 (arXiv 2505.00059). 98 professional actors recorded at home on smartphones, 19 phone positions, three vocal intensity levels (speak, raise voice, shout), 13 nonsense phrases covering all phonemes. Release quality issues (2026-10-23): (1) 31 groups, 82 clips of byte-identical audio (24 groups: the same sound in different recordings of the same speaker, emotion and phrase; 2 groups: different chunks of the same recording; 5 groups: carry metadata of different speakers, emotions or phrases, one of them spanning valid and test). (2) Some clips still contain all three vocal levels (A, B, C) in one file (the phrase repeated three times; the recordist apparently recorded the three levels together and forgot to cut them). (3) Some start with the spoken emotion name ("Anger."). (2) and (3) were found from Whisper transcripts of the 86 clips longer than 6 s; the ~4,437 clips of 6 s or less were not checked. Trimming individual clips would make them usable, but by the maintainer's decision the problems are only documented in the readme. The recipe uses 4,460 clips after removing the 63 duplicates, conflicting and multi-take clips. 3,704 clips at 48 kHz and 819 at 44.1 kHz, mono 16-bit, 1.028-22.528 s, 3.7248 h in total. Official split (train 78, valid 10, test 10 speakers; no speaker overlap).

label_basis_note: Cut from public YouTube videos; the distributor calls them "authentic emotional expressions" (kind of video unknown). The labelling procedure is not described.
notes: 2026 (v3, 2026-03-17). Natural emotional expressions collected from public YouTube videos. figshare 30218872 version 3 (2026-03-17). Bengali emotional speech from public YouTube videos. 5,215 clips, 7 emotions (745 each), all 3.0 s, 44.1 kHz mono 16-bit, 4.3458 h in total. Only gender is in the file names (Male 3,446 / Female 1,769; strongly skewed, e.g. only 16 Female for Angry); no speaker IDs, video IDs or transcripts. The labelling procedure is not documented. At least 50 pairs (100 clips) are near-identical (waveform correlation > 0.99, lag within +/-10 ms, different bytes; 3 pairs have different labels, 21 span train / valid / test). The report to the maintainer said 49 pairs (98 clips) and 20 cross-split pairs, but the DB maintainer re-ran the search over all clips and found one missed pair, Surprise_450_Male and Surprise_458_Male (correlation 0.9976, spanning train and test) (2026-10-23). Partial overlaps from shifted cuts (3-second windows of the same video) were not searched. The recipe uses the data as is (maintainer's decision).

name: CaFE
full_title: Canadian French Emotional (CaFE) speech dataset

notes: Canadian French Emotional (CaFE) speech dataset (ACM MMSys 2018, doi 10.1145/3204949.3208121), Zenodo 1478765. Six sentences pronounced by six male and six female actors in six basic emotions, each at two intensities (mild 'Faible' and strong 'Fort'), plus one neutral emotion: 936 wav. Recorded at 192 kHz 24-bit with a filtered 48 kHz 16-bit version; the recipe uses the 48 kHz one (mono, 2.557-7.745 s, 1.1549 h). A listening test was not found in the Zenodo description, the README or the abstract; the paper's full text could not be fetched.

name: CapSpeech
full_title: CapSpeech: Enabling Downstream Applications in Style-Captioned Text-to-Speech
license_note: The card puts all resources under CC BY-NC 4.0.
notes: Wang et al. (arXiv 2506.02863). Over 10 million machine-annotated pairs for pre-training; 358,783 human-annotated pairs for SFT (existing annotations of LibriTTS-R, VCTK, VoxCeleb, VoxCeleb2, EARS and Expresso, collected and refined with an LLM). New recordings include CapSpeech-AgentDB (capspeech_agentdb) and SEDB with sound effects.

name: CapSpeech-AgentDB
full_title: CapSpeech-AgentDB
license_note: Hugging Face license tag: CC BY-NC 4.0.
notes: For AgentTTS in CapSpeech (arXiv 2506.02863). One professional female voice actor performed lines and captions generated with GPT-4o-mini. 500 pairs are set aside for testing. Captions and splits are in OpenSound/CapSpeech-AgentDB and the AgentDB split of OpenSound/CapSpeech.

name: CASIA
license_note: Paid license from ChineseLDC (page archived 2020-05-01: domestic research CNY 5,000, domestic commercial 15,000, foreign research 35,000, foreign commercial 105,000). Terms as of 2024 unverified (the site could not be reached). None of the sources read allows free redistribution. The license field of the original AI Studio upload of the 1,200-clip version says 其他 (other); the LICENSE file of the Hugging Face mirror is 0 bytes.
labels_discrete_note: The 2010 edition (9,600 sentences) states only the number, 六种情绪 (six emotions), without listing them. The 2005 annotation guide has 5 emotions (高兴, 悲哀, 生气, 惊吓, 中性), which does not match six. The 1,200-clip version has 6 emotions (angry, fear, happy, neutral, sad, surprise), consistent between the file names and the AI Studio description.
label_basis_note: Speakers (2 male, 2 female) read identical sentences and emotion-revealing sentences in each emotion (ChineseLDC 2005 annotation guide). Labels are the target emotion read. No listening check is described. The same holds for the 1,200-clip version used by the recipe.
notes: "CASIA汉语情感语料库" (CASIA Chinese emotional speech corpus) of the Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (ChineseLDC CLDC-SPC-2005-010, developed 2005, added to ChineseLDC 2008-06-11, updated 2010-10-09). Acted speech: 4 professional speakers (2 male, 2 female) read identical sentences and sentences whose meaning reveals the emotion, with emotion; 16 kHz, 16-bit PCM. The size differs by edition (2005 catalogue: 6 emotions, 12,000 sentences / annotation guide: 5 emotions, 10,000 sentences; resource page updated 2010: 6 emotions, 9,600 sentences). The full corpus includes .tag files with syllable boundaries and F0. No paper by the creators was found. Tao, Liu, Zhang, Jia, "Design of Speech Corpus for Mandarin Text to Speech" (Blizzard Challenge 2008), cited by SER papers, describes a single-female-speaker 5,000-sentence speech-synthesis corpus and does not mention emotion (full text read). The 1,200-clip version used by EmoBox and others (4 speakers x 6 emotions x sentence numbers 201-250) was re-uploaded on 2023-04-16 to Baidu AI Studio (dataset 209512) by an individual (display name 千鹤) who is not the creator. The recipe's Hugging Face mirror (Bill13579/casia-mirror, created 2025-06-29, LICENSE 0 bytes) holds the same files: size and modification time match the 20 files shown on AI Studio (not checked by hash). No statement allowing free redistribution was found. Full investigation: reports/2026-10-23_casia_db_update.md.

name: CAVES
notes: Western Sydney University. 10 speakers x 50 sentences x 7 expressions = 3,500 AV recordings (the paper's 10,425 is the total of stimuli over three conditions: AV, video only and audio only).

name: C-BESD
full_title: Children-Bilingual Emotion Speech Dataset
license_note: Kaggle license field: CC BY-SA 4.0 (checked by the maintainer on 2026-10-23; the DB maintainer also checked via the API). The description says nothing about consent for recording children; by the maintainer's decision the license is the basis.
label_basis_note: Children aged 6-12 read simple sentences in each emotion (recorded with SurveyLex). Labels are the emotion recorded (folder and file names). No listening check is described.
notes: Kaggle `pranuthi19/bilingual-emotion-speech-datasetbesd` (version 1, 2024-02-07, author pranuthi_19). 70 children aged 6-12 (35 boys, 35 girls; 10 per age), native Telugu speakers learning English as a second language, recorded with SurveyLex. Telugu and English, 6 emotions, 5 utterances per emotion. File names `child number.language+gender_age_emotion_utterance number` (stated in the description). The description gives both 4,320 and 4,200 utterances; 4,320 is an arithmetic slip, since its own formula (35 x 2 x 5 x 6 x 2) gives 4,200. It also says 30 utterances per child, while the formula implies 60. The release has 4,204 wav files, 48 kHz stereo 16-bit, 3.0321 h in total (the description says about 2.5 h). The same child number appears only in some emotion folders, so recordings cannot be grouped by child. 36 groups (75 files) are byte-identical: 10 groups cross emotion folders (9 are misplaced folder copies, 1 is the same sound under neutral and sad) and 1 is " - Copy". The remaining 25 groups (52 files) share a label; 23 carry different child numbers, 5 of them different ages (e.g. neutral utterances 1-5 exist both for child 50, age 8, and child 70, age 7). Which is correct cannot be told from the release (2026-10-23). The recipe uses 4,164 clips after removing the 13 misplaced, " - Copy" and cross-label files and the 27 second-or-later copies within same-label groups.

name: Czech Database of Speech Emotions (CDSE)
notes: Values are from KuralHub and not confirmed in a primary source.

name: CEMO
language_note: The paper does not state the language. A French medical emergency call centre (agreement between APHP and LIMSI-CNRS); fillers are written as the French "euh"
labels_discrete_note: Fine-grained classes: 20 + Neutral (Fear, Anxiety, Stress, Panic, Anger, HotAnger, ...). The value lists the 8 coarse classes
notes: Devillers & Vidrascu (Interspeech 2006, pp. 801-804). 688 real calls to a medical emergency call centre (7 agents; callers 271 male, 513 female). Annotated by 2 experts. The paper's experiments use 4 coarse classes: Relief, Anger, Fear, Sadness. Table I of the MSP-Podcast paper gives 688 speakers.

name: Chen Bimodal
notes: L. Chen, Joint processing of audio-visual information for the recognition of emotional expressions in human-computer interaction (PhD thesis, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, 2000). Table I of the MSP-Podcast paper gives 5h36m, 100 speakers, Acted, English.

name: CLESC
full_title: Crowd Labeled Emotions and Speech Characteristics
license_note: Hugging Face card: CC BY 4.0.

notes: Zadeh, Cao, Hessner, Liang, Poria, Morency (EMNLP 2020, pp. 1801-1812). 40,000 of 128,768 sentences from 4,000 YouTube monologue videos are annotated, each by 3 AMT workers. The CMU Multimodal SDK README calls it MOSEAS-WE1. The paper gives no total duration; hours_reported is from Table I of the MSP-Podcast paper.

name: CPED
full_title: CPED: A Large-Scale Chinese Personalized and Emotional Dialogue Dataset for Conversational AI
license_note: GitHub license field: Apache-2.0 (text and features).

name: CREMA-D
license_note: LICENSE.txt: the database is under the Open Database License 1.0 (ODbL) and any rights in individual contents under the Database Contents License 1.0 (DbCL) (re-read in the release, 2026-10-26).
label_basis_note: Main label = the emotion code in the file name (ANG, DIS, FEA, HAP, NEU, SAD) with an intensity code (LO, MD, HI, XX). The crowd ratings (audio only, video only, both; summaryTable.csv holds the majority vote and level per clip, tabulatedVotes.csv the votes) are not used by the recipe.
notes: Cao et al., IEEE Trans. Affective Computing 5(4), 2014. 91 actors (48 male, 43 female; ages 20-74) speaking 12 sentences (IEO, TIE, IOM, IWW, TAI, MTI, IWL, ITH, DFA, ITS, TSI, WSI) in 6 emotions and 4 levels (low, medium, high, unspecified). 7,442 wav (angry, disgust, fear, happy, sad 1,271 each; neutral 1,087). Five groups of identical sound within one actor: 1006 TIE (happy / neutral), 1013 WSI (disgust / sad), 1017 IWW (angry / fear), 1067 IEO (disgust / fear), and 1045 ITH / IWL (same emotion, different sentences); recorded here and kept (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-26; from the review, not recomputed). Sentences are shared with SES-ED. The paper was not read; the README is the source.

name: Crowdsourcing Emotional Speech
labels_discrete_note: happy is split in two by arousal
notes: Smith, Tsiartas, Wagner, Shriberg, Bassiou (SRI International, ICASSP 2018, pp. 5139-5143). Participants recorded themselves with their own devices through a web tool (60% with built-in laptop microphones). Emotional speech was improvised while recalling past experiences; each participant also recorded non-emotional speech and read speech. Median recording length 7 s. 86,904 emotional and 23,164 non-emotional recordings.

name: CSEMOTIONS
full_title: CSEMOTIONS: High-Quality Mandarin Emotional Speech Dataset
language_note: Mandarin Chinese. Speakers are native Mandarin speakers
license_note: The card and LICENSE say Apache-2.0. The repository's NOTICE (pinned commit 19498e62...) says it incorporates Emotional-Speech-Data (ESD, MIT) that "can only be used for research purpose", but does not say which clips, and the card does not mention ESD. No clip overlaps in sound with any of ESD's 35,000 clips (re-checked by the DB maintainer, 2026-10-23), and no sentence is close to ESD's 350 Mandarin sentences (at most 19% character-bigram overlap). The Marco-Voice report describes CSEMOTIONS as new recordings and lists ESD as separate training data. The NOTICE may stem from the whole project, but the authors do not explain it. Treated as open by the maintainer's decision. Details: reports/2026-10-23_csemotions_db_update.md.
label_basis_note: 10 professional voice actors performed 7 emotions in a studio. Labels are the emotions performed (emotion column). Neither the card nor the paper describes checking labels by listening (the paper's listening tests evaluate synthesised speech).
notes: Alibaba AIDC-AI (named ATH-MaaS on Hugging Face). Released with the Marco-Voice technical report (arXiv 2508.02038). Studio recordings of 10 professional voice actors (5 male, 5 female), 7 emotions (neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprise, playfulness, fearful), 4,160 clips, 10.1978 h (measured), 1.752-34.212 s, 48 kHz mono 16-bit (the card says 24-bit; measured 16-bit). The `text` column holds the script sentence; 1,293 of 1,296 sentences are read by several speakers. Every sentence occurs under one emotion only, so the emotion can be read from the meaning (the maintainer listened to 4 clips per emotion and judged that the voice also differs by emotion, but a model may still use the meaning). No duplicates. The card's column names (transcript / speaker_id / gender / prompt_id) differ from the actual columns (audio / text / emotion / speaker). The paper says each speaker read 100 Chinese and English prompts, but the data has 1,296 distinct Chinese sentences. The paper's evaluation prompts are 100 per emotion (English and Chinese). For the NOTICE that mentions ESD, see license_note and reports/2026-10-23_csemotions_db_update.md.

name: DAIC-WOZ
full_title: Distress Analysis Interview Corpus - Wizard of Oz
language_note: The distribution page does not state the language (language value not filled)
license_note: Distributed only to academic and non-profit researchers because of consent restrictions (distribution page).
notes: Part of DAIC by Gratch et al. (USC ICT, LREC 2014). 189 interview sessions with the virtual interviewer Ellie (remotely operated by a person), 7-33 min (mean 16 min). The extended E-DAIC was used in AVEC 2019.

name: DailyTalk
full_title: DailyTalk: Spoken Dialogue Dataset for Conversational Text-to-Speech
language_note: English. Two actors fluent in English who had lived in the US for at least 3 years
license_note: The README says data and code are freely available for academic use under CC-BY-SA 4.0 (the repository license field says MIT).
release_version: GitHub release (link in the README, downloaded 2026-10-20)
labels_discrete_note: Inherits DailyDialog's labels (no emotion, anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness, surprise). Values per the DailyDialog paper
label_basis_note: Two voice actors fluent in English recorded DailyDialog dialogues as conversations in a studio and were directed to follow each utterance's emotion label. Those labels are DailyDialog's annotations of the text (from context and meaning), which DailyTalk inherits. No listening check is described.
notes: Lee, Park, Kim (KAIST, arXiv 2207.01063, ICASSP 2023). Conversational (dialogue-structured) speech data. 2,541 dialogues selected from DailyDialog were recorded in a studio by two voice actors fluent in English, as real conversations (not read verbatim from the script; they were directed to follow each utterance's emotion label). The release has 23,773 wav files (44.1 kHz, 16-bit; 23,720 mono, 53 stereo) and metadata.json, 21.6740 h in total. 7 labels (no emotion 18,966, happiness 3,856, surprise 407, sadness 301, anger 159, disgust 66, fear 18). metadata.json gives dialogue number, turn order, topic (1-10), dialogue act (inform 10,611, question 7,050, directive 3,741, commissive 2,371), transcript and speaker (0 / 1). The paper counts dialogues with added fillers (uh, um) as 962 for speaker 0 and 689 for speaker 1 (the release does not mark which). The paper says dialogues with more than 5 turns were selected, but the shortest dialogue in the data has 5 utterances. One utterance uses the same recording in two dialogues (d1121-u009 and d1253-u009, byte-identical), and 4 pairs of dialogues have identical text (177 and 532, 288 and 1698, 507 and 1383, 1069 and 2047; recorded separately).

name: Deeply Korean read speech corpus
license_note: OpenSLR page: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The full corpus is under a commercial license from Deeply Inc.
notes: Deeply Inc. (Korea, SLR97). Two speakers read scripts of three text polarities in three vocal polarities. Three locations (anechoic room, studio apartment, dance studio), 0.4/2.0/4.0 m, iPhone X and Galaxy S7. The full corpus is about 290 hours and 190,000 utterances; the public part about 3 hours and 2,000 utterances.

name: Deeply Nonverbal Vocalization Dataset
language_note: Non-verbal sounds by members of the Korean public
license_note: OpenSLR page: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The full corpus is under a commercial license from Deeply Inc.
notes: Deeply Inc. (Korea). Crowd-recorded on Android smartphones, 16 kHz. Public part: about 0.6 h, 800 vocalisations, 500 speakers; full corpus: about 57 h, 70,000, 1,500 speakers. Metadata on age, gender, noise and quality.

name: DFEW
full_title: Dynamic Facial Expression in-the-Wild
language_note: Clips from over 1,500 films. The language breakdown is not given
license_note: Non-commercial research only. Copying, redistribution and commercial use are prohibited (internal copies at a single site of the same organisation are allowed). States that the clips come from the internet and are not owned by AIPL (Southeast University).
source_rights_note: The terms state that the clips come from the Internet and are not the lab's property; no permission from the owners is documented. Needs a rights check (needs-confirmation list); license_class keeps the stated license.
notes: Southeast University AIPL (contacts Xingxun Jiang, Yuan Zong). Each clip classified into one of 7 facial expressions by 10 annotators. Videos with audio; some studies use the audio.

name: DIHANA
full_title: DIHANA corpus
notes: The first 11,911 entries of the archive were downloaded and checked (download stopped part-way). .ul files are per-utterance audio. The annotation formats (.cad .cwd .dia .dis .xml) were not read.

name: Dusha
full_title: Dusha: Large Raw Emotional Dataset with Aggregation Mechanism
license_note: Public license 'with attribution and conditions reserved' (Golos/Dusha license PDF): a reworking of CC BY-SA 4.0 with no non-commercial clause; attribution, indication of changes and share-alike. Not a Creative Commons license; treated as open by the maintainer's decision (2026-10-26). The podcast part is distributed as links only because of source-audio restrictions.
labels_discrete_note: happiness/positive, sadness, anger, neutral
source_rights_note: The crowd part (used) was recorded for the corpus. The podcast part is distributed only as links because of source-audio restrictions and is not used by the recipe.
notes: Dusha (Sber), arXiv 2212.12266; crowd 201,850 clips from 2,068 speakers (about 255 h) with audio, podcast part (303,963 total, 346.6 h in all) distributed as links only. The recipe uses the crowd part (crowd.tar, about 30 GB): the official lists give 160,366 clips (train 146,715 + test 13,651, 202.5 h before exclusions); 160,357 after dropping 9 clips of 4 same-sound groups with different emotions. 1,517 train clips are control tasks (known answer, no speaker or text id). source_id is a speaker id and does not overlap between train and test. Nine same-sound groups exist (5 with the same emotion, 4 with different emotions); the 5 same-emotion groups are removed only with exclude_duplicates true (default false; 160,352 clips). positive is renamed happy. The dataset's own agreement with the intended emotion is 71.5%; for intended sad, 51% became neutral (project review).

name: Egyptian-Arabic emotional speech corpus
full_title: Building an Egyptian-Arabic Speech Corpus for Emotion Analysis Using Deep Learning
notes: Safwat, Salem, Sharaf(LNCS 2023)。

name: EARS
full_title: EARS: An Anechoic Fullband Speech Dataset Benchmarked for Speech Enhancement and Dereverberation
language_note: English. Speakers' native language: US English 97, no answer 3, other 7 (speaker_statistics.json)
license_note: The README and LICENSE file say data and code are released under CC BY-NC 4.0 (GitHub API classifies it as NOASSERTION).
labels_discrete_note: emo_* in transcripts.json: adoration, amazement, amusement, anger, confusion, contentment, cuteness, desire, disappointment, disgust, distress, embarassment (original spelling), extasy (same), fear, guilt, interest, neutral, pain, pride, realization, relief, sadness, serenity
notes: Richter et al. (Interspeech 2024), Meta Reality Labs and Universität Hamburg. 100 hours in an anechoic room at 48 kHz. Also includes 7 reading styles (regular, loud, whisper, high/low pitch, fast, slow), free monologues and conversations. One zip per speaker p001-p107 (about 0.6 GB each). Speaker age, ethnicity, gender, height, weight and native language are provided.

name: EEKK
license_note: See the EESC row (figshare: CC BY 4.0).

name: EESC
full_title: Estonian Emotional Speech Corpus
license_note: figshare: CC BY 4.0. META-SHARE (doi:10.15155/EKI.000A) says Licence CC-BY (no version) and Availability: Available - Restricted Use.
label_basis_note: At least 30 Estonians over 30 who had lived in Estonia heard each sentence in isolation, without the text, and chose sadness, anger, joy or neutral; a sentence counts as identified when more than 50% chose the same (908 of 1,234). The listeners understood the words. Per-sentence identification rates are on the corpus site, not in the figshare release. How the release labels the 326 sentences without a majority is not described.
notes: Altrov & Pajupuu (ES3 workshop at LREC 2012, pp. 50-53), Institute of the Estonian Language (Eesti Keele Instituut); Estonian name Eesti emotsionaalse kõne korpus (EEKK). One female reader, chosen for articulation, a pleasant voice and empathy, read 130 journalistic passages without being told an emotion; the passages had been chosen because readers agreed they carried joy, anger or sadness. The passages were cut into sentences, and each sentence's label was set by a listening test (see label_basis_note). The paper also describes a text-only reading test that flags whether content may have influenced identification; the corpus site (peeter.eki.ee:5000, unreachable on 2026-10-24) shows that flag and per-sentence rates, the figshare release does not. Release: 1,164 wav (44.1 kHz mono 16-bit, 1.0850 h, 0.445-14.011 s) with TextGrids (tiers phoneme, word, sentence, emotion; 469 also have pos). Labels in the release: neutral 338, anger 306, joy 271, sadness 249, which do not match the paper's identified counts (joy 232, anger 277, sadness 191, neutral 208; 326 unidentified). 1,083 distinct sentence texts: 80 occur more than once (161 clips) and 27 of those carry different labels (e.g. 'Nii enda kui ka teiste puhul.' as neutral and anger). No byte-identical files.

name: Chinese Elderly emotion database (EESDB)
notes: Values are from KuralHub and not confirmed in a primary source. 8 elderly men and 8 elderly women (KuralHub).

name: EM2LDL
source_rights_note: The corpus integrates spontaneous emotional expressions from online platforms (README); no statement on rights in that material. Needs a rights check (needs-confirmation list); license_class keeps the stated license.

name: Emilia with Emotion Annotations
language_note: English 139.0k hours, Chinese 50.3k, German 7.2k, French 8.8k, Japanese 2.8k, Korean 7.5k (card)
license_note: The YAML of the card (laion/Emolia) says CC-BY-4.0. LAION's own paper (arXiv 2609.32016) gives CC-BY-NC-4.0 for the Emilia part and CC-BY-4.0 for the Emilia-YODAS part, and says derivatives inherit the license of the source clips. The original amphion/Emilia-Dataset terms are split the same way. Most naturally read as different licenses per part.
notes: LAION. Split into 5 Hugging Face repositories (...Annotations, ...2 to ...5), WebDataset format. About 215,600 hours. Sources disagree on the clip count: the paper arXiv 2609.32016 gives 71.78M clips and 215,600 hours; the laion/emolia-balanced-5M-subset card gives 80.5M samples. Derivatives: laion/emolia-balanced-5M-subset (5,256,683 items, balanced by thresholds on the 40 emotion scores and speaker clusters), laion/emolia-voicenet-gemini-annotations (468,180 annotations of 236,613 clips by Gemini 3.5 Flash).

name: EMIS
full_title: Emotionally Incongruent Synthetic Speech Dataset
license_note: Zenodo record license: GPL-3.0-or-later (checked by the maintainer, 2026-10-24). The audio was synthesised from ESD reference voices by three TTS systems; the record and the paper do not discuss their terms. Read on 2026-10-24: ESD has an MIT LICENSE file, but its README asks users to sign a license form and says the database can only be used for research purpose. The F5-TTS code is MIT while its pre-trained models are CC-BY-NC (trained on Emilia, CC BY-NC-4.0 with YODAS part CC BY 4.0, access requires accepting conditions). CosyVoice2 code and model are Apache-2.0 on the model card, but its paper says the training data came from internal tools and does not name the sources. StyleTTS2 code is MIT; its README asks users of the pre-trained models to tell listeners that speech is synthesised unless the voice owner permitted it. Which checkpoints EMIS used, and how model terms reach generated audio, is not stated. Whether GPL-3.0-or-later overrides these conditions is not stated either.
label_basis_note: Label = the voice emotion requested of the TTS system, taken from the emotion of the ESD reference audio (the third field from the end of the file name). Not perceived: the release has no per-clip listener data. The paper's 40-listener check covers a balanced subset only (identification of the reference emotion 39.4-62.0% for the three TTS systems, 70.8% for ground-truth samples; arXiv v2, ICASSP version not seen).
notes: Corrêa, Lima, Moreno, Ueda, Costa (UNICAMP). Paper: arXiv 2510.25054 (Zenodo links the ICASSP 2026 DOI 10.1109/ICASSP55912.2026.11462441, whose text was not seen). Synthetic speech. 104 emotion-rich sentences written by GPT-4.5 (the Zenodo record says ChatGPT-4.5): per emotion (angry, happy, sad) explicit and implicit sentences, plus neutral sentences; each was synthesised in four voice emotions (angry, happy, neutral, sad) by F5-TTS, CosyVoice2 and StyleTTS2 (named in the paper; file names say F5TTS, COSY, STYLE). Reference audio: for each generation one of the 10 ESD English speakers (0011-0020) was drawn at random and their 7 longest utterances concatenated (about 30 s). 1,248 files (416 per TTS), 24 kHz mono, 1.2629 h, 1.824-8.107 s; F5TTS files are PCM_16 and the others float. 936 files have a voice emotion different from the text emotion and 312 are congruent. 26 sentence groups (number at the start of the file name): groups 01-13 hold six emotional sentences and one neutral sentence, groups 14-26 one neutral sentence each. No byte-identical files. text_samples_EMIS.csv in the record lists the sentences. The 'ground-truth' samples of the paper's listening check are not described. EMIS derives its reference voices from ESD (no relation row: the vocabulary has no derived_from type).

name: EMNS
license_note: OpenSLR 136 page: License Apache 2.0 (re-read 2026-10-26; checked by the maintainer).
labels_discrete_note: happy, sad, angry, excited, sarcastic, neutral, disgusted and surprised

name: EmoFilm
source_rights_note: Clips cut from 43 films (English originals and Italian / Spanish dubs). The Zenodo record is restricted, states no license and does not discuss rights in the films. Needs a rights check; license_class keeps the stated license.

name: EmoGator
full_title: EmoGator: A New Open Source Vocal Burst Dataset
license_note: GitHub license field: Apache-2.0.
label_basis_note: Label = the category of the prompt the contributor was answering (the speaker's intent). No listener ratings exist. Quality control by one person (the paper's author): silent or noise-only submissions and readings of category names were handled, problematic samples re-recorded, and contributors who did not convey distinct emotions left out (how many is not stated).
notes: Fred W. Buhl (University of Florida, arXiv 2301.00508). Unpaid volunteers and Mechanical Turk workers recorded each of 30 categories 3 times (90 per person) after reading prompts that describe a situation for the category (a modified and expanded version of the prompts of the Hume-VB study; listed in the paper's online supplement, which was not read), on a website using their own devices. Files are mp3 (the paper says 44.1 or 48 kHz; measured 48 kHz mono 30,334, 48 kHz stereo 1,706, 44.1 kHz mono 90), 0.420-2.040 s, 16.7667 h measured (the paper says 16.9654 h, possibly a different way of measuring mp3 length). File names are <six-digit contributor ID>-<category 01-30>-<take 1-3>. 357 contributors with 90 files each; 1,071 files per category. 20 byte-identical pairs (same contributor and category, different takes). All participants gave informed consent and the procedure was approved by the University of Florida IRB (paper). The author warns of a bias toward North American English speakers' expressions. Contributor sex, age, language and origin are not in the release. Efforts were made to avoid one person contributing twice, without a guarantee. The paper suggests the data could be used to measure how often listeners identify the intended category.

name: Emolah
notes: Values are from KuralHub and not confirmed in a primary source. KuralHub gives the license as Creative Commons Attribution and the recordings as spontaneous. About 4 hours.

name: EmoNet-Voice
full_title: EmoNet-Voice: A Fine-Grained, Expert-Verified Benchmark for Speech Emotion Detection
language_note: 4 languages (paper abstract; the languages are not named there)
license_note: The card of the Hugging Face repository holding Bench (an anonymous review account, t1a5anu-anon) says CC BY 4.0. No official LAION-owned location was found.
labels_discrete_note: 40 fine-grained emotion categories and intensity
notes: Schuhmann et al. (LAION, 2025). EmoNet-Voice Big is synthetic speech for pre-training (the abstract says 5,000 hours; the per-language sum in Table 2 is 4,752 hours; Table 1 says >1M items and >4,500 hours). EmoNet-Voice Bench is an evaluation set of 12,600 items (36.26 hours) chosen from Big; 6 experts (psychology bachelor or higher) gave 33,605 ratings (2-4 per item). The abstract's 4.7k is the unanimous part. Inter-rater Cronbach's alpha is 0.14. It includes, through synthesis, emotions that are hard to collect from people, such as pain and shame. Distributed through the paper's Hugging Face collection laion/emonet: emonet-voice-bench (12,600 items, CC-BY-4.0) and emonet-voice-foundation under the anonymous account t1a5anu-anon. The foundation card points to laion/laions_got_talent_enhanced_flash_annotations_and_long_captions as the main data. The paper says it is released as a research artefact for academic use.

name: EMOSEC
license_note: Zenodo license field: CC BY 4.0 (captions).
notes: Creator: Anonymous Authors. File: merged_file.json (about 30 MB). Data made by AlignCap (arXiv 2410.19134): about 41 hours of Chinese and English emotion captions, 15 male and 15 female speakers, 45,039 sentences, 16 kHz. The speaker make-up matches ESD (20) + IEMOCAP (10).

name: EmoSpeech (keyword)
language_note: Keywords (help, bacho, stop, ...). Language not stated
license_note: Kaggle license field: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The bundled License.txt is Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International, and the paper says the data is released for non-commercial purposes (checked by the maintainer, 2026-10-24).
label_basis_note: Label = the emotion displayed to the speaker (calm, happy, angry, fearful). Reviewers matched each recording against reference samples (paper Section 4.4); no ratings are distributed. The `background` class carries the same emotion tags although it holds no speech.
notes: Indian EmoSpeech Command Dataset (Banga, Upadhyay, Agarwal, Sharma, Mukherjee, arXiv 1910.13801, 2019). Kaggle ujjwal9/emospeech (free account). 3-second commands recorded on phones in real surroundings (house, metro, roads, railway, near a lake, ...), each with a keyword, an emotion and an environment sound. Keyword classes: help, bachao (spelled bacho in the files), stop, go, yes, no, `unknown` (any other word) and `background` (sound whose source is not human vocal chords, e.g. birds or road noise; paper Section 5). Emotions: calm, happy, angry, fearful, and a tag None. Environment tag in the file name: safe, scream, glass break, gunshots (the README does not list scream). Collection: Android app, then a game-like web app; 250 speakers (paper); privacy-policy consent. Quality control: samples whose word reviewers cannot tell are rejected, each sample is checked by two people, and emotion is matched against reference samples (Section 4.4). Release: 7,735 wav (16 kHz mono 16-bit, 1.963-3.755 s, 6.5486 h), README.md, License.txt; names are keyword-environment-emotion-timestamp-hash.wav; 89 groups of byte-identical files (179 files, 90 redundant). `background` has 1,116 clips (calm 880, None 163, fearful 53, happy 19, angry 1); `None` has 164 clips, 163 of them background. The hash field has 103 values and does not match the paper's 250 speakers. Language is not stated (English and Hindi words).

name: EMOSpeech (SECap)

name: EmoTale
full_title: EmoTale: An Enacted Speech-emotion Dataset in Danish
license_note: The repository (snehadas/EmoTale, commit 41e7d00f) has no LICENSE file and GitHub shows no license. The datasheet answers 'Will the dataset be distributed under a copyright or other IP license?' with: 'The data will be distributed under a copyright. There is no license, but there is a request to cite the corresponding paper if the dataset is used.' The project treats the request to cite the paper as the terms of use (the maintainer's decision, 2026-10-26), as for IESC, so the class is open. The authors have not been asked; confirming with them is optional.
label_basis_note: Main label = the emotion the participant was asked to enact (file name; equals gt_emotion in annotations.csv for all 800). In addition, three annotators (the first, second and last authors of the paper) independently gave each utterance a categorical emotion and arousal, valence and dominance on a 1-5 scale in 0.5 steps; these are in annotations.csv and agree with the enacted emotion in 639, 706 and 507 of 800 cases. Cohen's kappa against the enacted emotion is 0.75 and 0.85 for annotators 1 and 2 (paper Table II). All three agree in 465 clips, at least two in 749 (113 of them differ from the enacted emotion), and none agree in 51.
notes: Hjuler, Skat-Rørdam, Clemmensen, Das (DTU, ASRU 2025, arXiv 2508.14548; collected as part of a master's thesis). Enacted speech in Danish and English. Participants with acting experience were recruited (age at least 7, Danish speakers); recorded in quiet rooms with wireless Rode microphones at 48 kHz (stereo 16-bit wav in the release). 18 participants (12 female, 6 male, 9-39 years, mean 22.8; 3 are children aged 9-12) enacted 5 emotionally neutral sentences (translated from Emo-DB) in 5 emotions (anger, happiness, sadness, boredom, neutral), self-inducing the emotion by recalling a situation; only the last take was kept. 800 clips (450 Danish, 350 English), 160 per emotion, 1.070-7.443 s, 0.6170 h. File names: language_speaker_emotion_sentence (e.g. DK_004_A_5.wav). Written consent under GDPR, IRB approval (documents in the repository). The label is the enacted emotion; annotations.csv additionally holds three annotators' perceived categories and arousal-valence-dominance ratings (the annotators are three authors of the paper). The README says two annotators; the paper reports agreement between annotators 1 and 2 and the file holds three. The datasheet warns that the dataset is small and not suited for tasks needing large-scale training or natural emotional speech. The recipe does not use the perceived labels.

name: Emotional EMA
full_title: An articulatory study of emotional speech production
language_note: Native speakers of US English (Zenodo description and the zip's README)
license_note: Zenodo license field: CC BY 4.0 (registered 2026-03-29).
labels_discrete_note: The recipe's labels are the final labels derived from the listener evaluation (`<jn|jr|kf|pssg>_best_emo` in the zip; code 1 = neutral, 2 = angry, 3 = happy, 4 = sad, 5 = fear; the README does not explain the codes, which were read from the column order neu, ang, hap, sad, fea, oth of the evaluation files). They match the target emotion given to the speakers (file names) for 885 of 953 clips; 68 differ (fear -> angry 14, sad 6, neutral 4, happy 2; happy -> fear 9, neutral 9, sad 5, angry 2; etc.). Labels used: neutral 277, angry 182, sad 175, happy 160, fear 159.
label_basis_note: 3 speakers (2 female, 1 male) read sentences 5 times in each of 4 target emotions. Multiple raters evaluated categorical emotion (with confidence) and dimensions (valence, activation, dominance); the evaluation files are distributed. The number of raters and how ratings were combined are not described in detail in the release. The recipe uses the final evaluation label (*_best_emo), not the target emotion.
notes: EMA (electromagnetic articulography) corpus of USC SAIL. The Zenodo description gives the DOI of a 2005 paper and 4 emotions, 680 utterances, 10 sentences for women and 14 for the man, but the zip holds 5 emotions, 956 wav files (3 of them dummies), 8 sentences + 2 passages, which does not match. 3 speakers (jn, jr = female, kf = male). The zip's README says the speaker IDs (F1, F2, M1) are the same as in USC-EMO-MRI (possibly the same people; which corresponds to which is not documented; recorded here because relations has no suitable type; the maintainer judged it fine to include both in a multi-corpus set, 2026-10-22). wav are 22.05 kHz mono 16-bit (not the 16 kHz the README says); the 953 used clips are 1.359-63.0 s, 1.63 h in total. All 953 have listener evaluations (11, 13 or 15 ratings per utterance: per-listener emotion, strength and confidence, vote totals, final label). Articulatory data (tongue, lip and jaw positions, 100 Hz) come as `.mat` files.

The Hugging Face page counts (neutral 6,853 and so on) are those of the audio+video (multimodal) labels, not of the audio labels. Audio-label counts (recipe, json audio field; paper section 3.3 agrees): neutral 9,378 / angry 3,820 / happy 2,105 / surprised 1,363 / sad 1,110 / disgusted 818 / fearful 656. 18,612 files are stereo (left and right mostly nearly identical) and 120 are 16 kHz; 6,647 utterances are marked as overlapping speech.

license_note: Zenodo license field: CC BY 4.0.

notes: Bastos Germano et al. (State University of Rio de Janeiro, 2021). 8 actors (4 male, 4 female) chose from 10 sentences and recorded them in 4 emotions: happiness 91, anger 94, sadness 100, neutral 92. File names: gender, actor ID, emotion, number. emouerj-sed (AdeoyeLadele) on Hugging Face has a similar name; relation unverified. Acted Portuguese speech from UERJ. Median F0: men 152-168 Hz, women 210-269 Hz. 377 wav files, 44.1 kHz stereo 16-bit (262 with identical channels, 115 with different ones), 1.188-7.094 s, 0.3150 h in total. File names `<m|w><actor ID><emotion><recording number>.wav`. The list of 10 sentences is on Zenodo, but the release does not say which file is which sentence. The Zenodo record cites no paper.

name: EmoV-DB
license_note: LICENSE.md in the corpus repository: 'Non-commercial Purposes' (research, teaching, scientific publication, personal experimentation); the GitHub license API returns NOASSERTION. A custom non-commercial license, so the class stays research_only. The maintainer confirmed it is non-commercial (2026-10-26). Distributed on OpenSLR 115.
notes: Speakers bea and jenie (female), josh and sam (male); the paper also describes a French male speaker who is not in the OpenSLR archives. josh has only amused, neutral and sleepy, so the speaker is a cue for the label (speaker-emotion confound). The archive is organised by speaker x emotion (18 archives); file names carry neither speaker nor emotion and the same name occurs in several archives. 44.1 kHz and 16 kHz are mixed; the recipe uses 6,893 files (9.49 h) converted to 16 kHz. The listing and the DB say 7,000 files; the real count is 6,893. Texts are based on the CMU Arctic sentences. No official split. No listening test was found in the sources read.

name: EMOVIE

license_note: The distribution page asks users to follow CC BY-NC-SA (the link points to the 2.0 legal code).

notes: Cui et al. (Interspeech 2021, pp. 2766-2770), Zhejiang University. Dialogue cut from 5.1/7.1-channel film audio. A dataset for emotional TTS. Distributed as a tar.gz on Google Drive (labels.csv has file name, label and text).

name: EMOVO
full_title: EMOVO Corpus: an Italian Emotional Speech Database
notes: Costantini et al., LREC 2014. Six actors (3 male, 3 female) x 14 sentences x 7 emotions = 588 files, 0.51 h; 48 kHz stereo (one file mono). Sentences 8-10 are nonsense sentences. Obtained from emovo.zip on the Google Drive linked from the official page (Internet Archive capture of 2023); the Kaggle copy is a third-party re-upload and is not used. The two microphone channels are offset by about 0.4-0.6 ms, so the left-right average used by the recipe has a notch near 1.2 kHz (project review; the effect on training is not measured). A listening test on two sentences gave 80% overall accuracy.

name: EmoVoice-DB
license_note: Hugging Face card: MIT (checked by the maintainer, 2026-10-24). All audio is synthesised with OpenAI's GPT-4o-audio. The GPT-4o System Card (arXiv 2410.21276) says the pre-training data are selected public data (mainly industry-standard machine-learning datasets and web crawls) and proprietary data from partnerships, with multimodal data including images, audio and video; it names no datasets or sources, so the rights to the voices it learned from are unknown. The OpenAI Services Agreement (version effective 2026-01-01; read on 2026-10-25) says that between customer and OpenAI the customer owns all Output (4.1), and that the customer may not use Output to develop AI models that compete with OpenAI products and services except for permitted exceptions (3.3(e)): models mainly for categorising or classifying data (such as embeddings or classifiers) that are not distributed or made commercially available to third parties, and fine-tuning offered by OpenAI. Which terms applied to the API use when EmoVoice-DB was made (early 2025), and whether training a speech emotion recognizer counts under these terms, is not stated in any source read. The card and the paper do not mention OpenAI's terms. The GitHub README of the EmoVoice model (as recorded earlier) says the model weights are CC-BY-NC because of the Emilia training data; that is separate from the data license.
label_basis_note: Label = the coarse emotion category paired with the fine-grained description used as the instruction to GPT-4o-audio. Not perceived by any listener; the card describes no emotion check (only WER filtering).
notes: Yang et al. (EmoVoice, arXiv 2504.12867, ACM MM 2025). English synthetic emotional speech; every clip generated by GPT-4o-audio. Steps (card and paper): (1) GPT-4o writes pairs of text (novel excerpts, dialogue, observations) and emotion description; (2) GPT-4o-audio is prompted with text and description (e.g. 'Repeat this sentence with the emotion of <description>: <text>') in one of 5 voices (ash, ballad, coral, sage, verse); (3) samples with high WER are removed; (4) GPT-4o rephrases each description twice, giving three descriptions per sample in train. 7 emotions: angry, happy, sad, surprised, disgusted, fearful, neutral. The official lists hold 22,100 clips (40.44 h; train 21,050, val 350, test 700; the train list has 63,150 rows because of the rephrasings); valid and test have equal counts per class. Archives: 24,923 wav (24 kHz mono 16-bit, 45.78 h, 1.05-59.6 s) in seven per-emotion zips, 2,823 of them in no list (5.34 h, all five voices; the reason is not stated). The five voices are synthetic timbres, not people. The Hugging Face repository also holds laions_got_latent.jsonl (203 MB), which the GitHub README of the model links to LAION's Got Talent; the recipe does not download it and no LAION file is among the wav. The card's text example for test.jsonl includes a neutral prompt speech file. Labels are the requested emotion, not perceived.

name: Emozionalmente

The expression is the actors' intention; evaluations (829 people, 5 per clip, with a good/bad audio-quality flag) are in metadata/evaluations.csv. The official speaker-independent split (stratified by emotion, gender and age) is in metadata/split/ and the recipe reads it. Actor attributes (gender, age, mother tongue) are in users.csv. Recordings use ordinary devices of the volunteers.

name: eNTERFACE
notes: eNTERFACE'05 audio-visual emotion database. The release holds 1,293 AVI files in 44 subject folders (the distribution page reports 42 subjects) with no accompanying document; the emotion and speaker are taken from directory names (file names contain 23 errors). 42 subjects have the expected 30 recordings (5 sentences x 6 emotions); subject 23 lacks 3 (happiness, sentences 1-3); subject 6 has one file per emotion of 56 to 107 s (Whisper transcripts: repetitions of the lines, the experimenter's instructions such as 'from the beginning' and retakes; no human check). Used 1,287 recordings: angry 215, disgust 215, fear 215, happy 212, sad 215, surprise 215. The spreadsheet's 1,166 utterances cannot be traced to any count of the release. Fixed sentences per emotion were checked by transcribing all clips of subjects 1 and 2. The previous recipe excluded subjects 6 and 23; the exclusion of 23 was not the maintainer's decision and was withdrawn.

license_note: Zenodo license field: CC BY 4.0. The description says "Anyone can use this data only for research purposes", which disagrees.

name: ESD
full_title: Emotional Speech Dataset (ESD)
license_note: Research use only. The GitHub page asks users to fill in the license form and send it to the authors; the repository's MIT license covers code, not the speech data. The maintainer's decision (2026-10-26): the form must be submitted before use (on the requires-application list).
notes: Zhou, Sisman, Liu, Li (Speech Communication 137, 2022). Mandarin (speakers 0001-0010) and English (0011-0020), 5 male and 5 female per language; 20 speakers x 5 emotions x 350 sentences. Download is a Google Drive zip (2.4 GB) without checksums (the file count is the only check). No duplicates by bytes, decoded audio or near match (project review). The zip carries no official split (the paper defines 20 evaluation, 30 test and the rest training utterances per speaker-emotion).

name: E-SERAVD
license_note: The Kaggle page says CC BY 4.0. However, the material is dialogue audio from Indonesian films, and it is unlikely that the film rights holders allow free use (maintainer's judgement, 2026-10-22). The author's license field is trusted and the class stays `open`, but the doubt is recorded.
release_version: Three Kaggle releases (versions 1, 1.1, 1.2). Version 1.2 (6 emotions) is used
labels_discrete_note: Labels come from ratings by 3 people; the emotion whose mean probability is highest and at least 0.67 is the main emotion (README of version 1.2). The 3,000 clips are 500 per emotion. The README's vote counts (disgust 42 votes, fear 908 votes) cannot account for the final 500 disgust and 500 fear clips, and the README does not describe how these emotions were rated (an arithmetic reading, not confirmed with the authors). The recipe uses 2,976 clips after removing 24 near-duplicates.
label_basis_note: Dialogue from 11 Indonesian films (performed by actors). Each clip was rated by 3 raters over 6 emotions, and the emotion with mean probability >= 0.67 (at least 2 of 3) became the final label. Fleiss' kappa = 0.6713. The README only says "each audio and video clip was evaluated"; whether raters heard the audio only or also watched the video cannot be told.
notes: EEPIS (Electronic Engineering Polytechnic Institute of Surabaya). Version 1.2 (3,000 clips, 6 emotions) cut from dialogue in 11 Indonesian films. The files are 44.1 kHz stereo 32-bit float (the Kaggle page's "16 kHz" is wrong; the bundled specification sheet also says 44.1 kHz). 0.833-7.5 s (mean 2.40 s), 1.999 h in total. No speaker, gender or transcript information. The Kaggle release contains three versions; versions 1 and 1.1 are the same 1,200 clips with 4 emotions, different from the 3,000 clips of 1.2. Comparing 350 wav files of version 1.1 with 1.2: of a random 200, 115 (57.5%) are byte-identical to 1.2 files, and 81 of those 115 have a different label (e.g. none of the 19 that were sad in 1.1 is sad in 1.2). In version 1.2, 12 pairs (24 clips) of nearly the same sound of the same line in the same film have different labels. name: Harper Valley Bank
full_title: Harper Valley Bank Spoken Dialog Corpus
license_note: The repository's `LICENSE` is the full text of Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International. "How to Cite" in the README gives the BibTeX of arXiv:2010.13929.
release_version: GitHub cricketclub/gridspace-stanford-harper-valley commit 0bd721e877c4a85d8c13ff837e68661ea6200a98 (2021-03-12). The recipe downloads the master tarball (676,302,876 bytes)
labels_discrete_note: Polarity, not emotion. Each segment's `emotion` is a softmax over negative/neutral/positive (summing to 1.0), and the arg-max is the label (ties to 0). Arg-max over all 25,730 segments: neutral 17,149 / positive 8,148 / negative 433. In the 19,456 segments used by the recipe (6,274 without speech removed): neutral 10,960 / positive 8,080 / negative 416. The median confidence (max probability) of negative arg-maxes is 0.492, a weak decision. positive is frequent in agents' greetings and closings, and some negative examples are lexically neutral (`i need to check my account balance`).
label_basis_note: Crowd workers were assigned the role of a bank customer or agent and talked by phone following a goal and a rough script (role-play, no emotion instruction). Sentiment polarity (negative / neutral / positive) is an automatic estimate by the Gridspace Speech API, not a human annotation.
notes: Wu, Nafziger, Scodary, Maas (Gridspace and Stanford). 1,446 simulated call-centre calls, 59 speakers (in agent and caller roles). One call = 2 wav files (one per side, 8 kHz mono PCM_16). Human transcripts by trained Gridspace Mixer workers. Segmentation follows the word times of Gridspace's automatic speech recognition (paper: "automatic segmentation"). In all 25,730 segments `duration_ms` matches the end of the last word of the machine transcript. Measured disagreements with the README: `duration_ms` is described as the call length but is the segment length; `offset_ms` does not match the audio position (`start_ms` does); `channel_index` (1 = caller, 2 = agent) and `speaker_role` are swapped in 37 calls (596 segments), and the voice is in the wav on the `channel_index` side (confirmed by listening and audio energy). Differences from Table 1 of the paper: words per utterance, paper mean 4.1 and median 4.5, measured (`human_transcript`) mean 5.64 and median 4.0; utterances per call, paper 2-60, measured 3-76 (the mean 17.79 matches). `hours_reported` 23.7 corresponds to the one-side total (measured 23.655 h); both sides total 47.311 h and segments total 12.024 h. 349 segments have an empty human transcript and 5,925 only tags such as `[noise]`. The corpus has no speaker gender, age or other attributes. Simulated calls (crowd workers phoning from scripts), with vocabulary limited to about 700 words: scripted, acted conversation rather than real customers' emotions. Labels are the output of Gridspace's automatic model, not human, and no human verification is described (neither the paper nor the README gives the model's name, version, training data or accuracy). Whether to use it for training or only for evaluation is the recipe side's (maintainer's) decision, still open.

name: IEMOCAP
label_basis_note: Label = the majority of at least three annotators' categorical evaluations (ground truth in the first line of each utterance summary; xxx when there is no majority). The evaluation files also hold dimensional ratings (valence, activation, dominance; at least two annotators) and the actors' self-evaluations. The recipe uses the ground truth with all codes, including xxx as the class no_majority.
notes: Busso et al., IEMOCAP, Language Resources and Evaluation 42(4), 2008. Audio, transcriptions, video and motion capture of five sessions of dyadic mixed-gender actor pairs (ten actors), scripted and improvised. Utterances were segmented manually and each was evaluated categorically over {angry, happy, sad, neutral, frustrated, excited, fearful, surprised, disgusted, other} by at least three annotators and dimensionally by at least two. Utterance counts by ground truth: xxx (no majority) 2,507; frustrated 1,849; neutral 1,708; angry 1,103; sad 1,084; excited 1,041; happy 595; surprise 107; fear 40; other 3; disgust 2 (10,039 in all; recounted from the recipe measurement). hap and exc are separate classes here. Two utterances are longer than 30 s and removed by remove_long_short. No official split; the recipe splits at random by utterance within each label (disgust only in train), so speakers appear in every split.

notes: Xin, Takamichi and Saruwatari (University of Tokyo, Speech Communication 156, 2024, 103004). Files are 48 kHz stereo 24-bit except one 22.05 kHz mono 16-bit file, 0.422-9.616 s, 0.3950 h; the readme states 406.9 s in total, which does not match. phrases.txt lists the 87 designated phrases; the phrases of the F session are not recorded. Sessions: regular (the nonverbal phrase is specified, 1,375 clips) and free (the speaker chooses the phrase, 240 clips). Scripts were generated with ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301) in a way that balances phonemes. A listening test (crowd, forced choice) gave 94.21% (87.37% without the nonverbal parts). transcription.csv has 514 rows; nv_label/ has the nonverbal intervals of 1,615 files (neither used by the recipe).

The extended laion/laions_got_talent_enhanced_flash_annotations_and_long_captions (no README, 1,510 files, 196.3 GB) adds Gemini Flash annotations and long descriptions, and the card of EmoNet-Voice Big (foundation) points to it as the main data. license_note: LDC license (terms for members and non-members).
