name: LEGOv2
license_note: license.txt in the release lists two licenses, both: 'Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to use this data and its documentation for individual, education research purposes only.' (Carnegie Mellon University, 2003-2015, for the recorded data and transcriptions; Ulm University, 2009-2015, for the annotations). Redistribution is not mentioned. The readme asks to cite Schmitt, Ultes and Minker (LREC 2012) and Ultes et al. (IWSDS 2015).
labels_discrete_note: friendly, neutral, slightly angry, angry, very angry (one rater, 302 calls). The release also contains 'garbage' (589 utterances), which is not in the scheme and is not used. Counts of the 4,832 labelled utterances: neutral 3,305; slightly angry 693; garbage 589; angry 137; very angry 104; friendly 4.
label_basis_note: One rater judged the callers' emotional state (friendly, neutral, slightly angry, angry, very angry) for 302 calls; the readme does not say whether the rater listened to the audio or read the dialogue. The release also holds a value 'garbage' (589 utterances) that the readme does not define; the maintainer listened to several and found silence or content that cannot be labelled, so the recipe leaves them out.
notes: Parameterized and annotated spoken dialogue corpus of the CMU Let's Go bus information system (Schmitt, Ultes and Minker, LREC 2012; Ultes et al., IWSDS 2015); interactions from 2006 and 2007, annotated at Ulm University. Archive 1.19 GB from the University of Bamberg server, no official checksum. 7,909 wav: user utterances (mostly 8 kHz mono 16-bit, one 44.1 kHz) and whole-call recordings up to 1,332 s. interactions.csv holds 13,835 exchanges with 53 interaction parameters, ASR results, dialogue acts and the emotional state; 4,832 have an emotion label and an audio file. The release also has Interaction Quality annotations (401 calls, 9,638 exchanges, several raters), calls.csv (gender, age, outcome per call), acoustics.csv (Praat features) and a MySQL dump, none of which the recipe uses. Utterances are short (median 1.1 s). Two groups of byte-identical files (533 files, copies of one call folder) are not among the used utterances. The language is English.

name: Lithuanian Emotional Speech Database (Emocijų duomenų bazė)
license_note: The repository (BPTI-LT/Emociju-duomenu-baze, commit 526844b9, last pushed 2018-05-03) has no LICENSE file and GitHub shows no license; the README holds a description only, with no license or citation request. Terms for research use, redistribution and commercial use are unknown. The maintainer will ask the authors (2026-10-25; not yet contacted) and, until then, does not redistribute or use it commercially.
labels_discrete_note: Folder names are Lithuanian: Baime (fear), Pyktis (anger), Dziaugsmas (happiness), Nuostaba (surprise), Pasislykstejimas (disgust), Liudesys (sadness), Neutrali (neutral). Speaker 5 also has a folder Ilgesys (9 clips), a word that means longing and is not among the README's seven emotions; the recipe uses it as an eighth class, longing (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-25).
label_basis_note: Label = the emotion the non-professional actor was reading in (folder name). The README describes no verification.
notes: Recorded in the study 'Let's teach the Computer to Feel (Recognize Emotions in the Human Voice)' of the Mokslo pieva project (BPTI-LT, 2018). 10 non-professional actors read 100 phrases in seven emotions (README). Archive of 1,453 wav (44.1 kHz mono 16-bit, 2.357-8.167 s, 1.6598 h) in folders EMOdb/<n> Zmogus/<n> <Emotion>/<Emotion>_<phrase number>.wav. Counts per speaker and emotion range from 4 to 98 (e.g. speaker 1: 98 Pyktis and 10 Baime; speaker 10: 94 Dziaugsmas). Class counts: sadness 342, happiness 260, neutral 245, anger 239, disgust 150, surprise 105, fear 103, longing 9. No gender, age or phrase texts are given. No byte-identical files.

name: M3ED
source_rights_note: Clips of 56 TV series (about 500 episodes). The GitHub repository states no license; the sources read say nothing about rights in the series. Needs a rights check; license_class keeps the stated license (none).

name: MAFW
full_title: MAFW: A Large-scale, Multi-modal, Compound Affective Database for Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition in the Wild
language_note: Clips from films, dramas and short videos from China, Japan, Korea, Europe, the US and India. The language breakdown is not given
license_note: Non-commercial research only. Copying, redistribution and commercial use are prohibited (internal copies at a single site of the same organisation are allowed).
labels_discrete_note: 11 single-expression classes and 32 compound-expression classes. An 11-dimensional distribution from the 11 annotators is also given. The labels are mainly for facial expression recognition
notes: Liu et al. (ACM MM 2022). 10,045 video clips with audio. Four benchmarks: single and compound expressions, unimodal and multimodal.

name: MAHNOB-HCI
labels_discrete_note: emotional keywords

name: Malayalam speech emotion dataset (ANN)
notes: Values are from KuralHub and not confirmed in a primary source. 340 male and 300 female utterances, 10 male and 8 female speakers, 8 kHz (KuralHub).

name: Maleo Emotion
full_title: Maleo Emotion Audio Dataset Indonesia
language_note: Some utterances mix in English and other languages, and some are entirely in a foreign language (card)
license_note: The source used is a copy. Rights in the original could not be checked beyond the CC BY 4.0 notice
labels_discrete_note: Folder names in Indonesian (Jijik, Marah, Netral, Sedih, Senang, Takut, Terkejut)
source_rights_note: The clips are cut from YouTube videos. The data card states CC BY 4.0 but says nothing about the rights in the videos, and there is no paper. Needs a rights check (needs-confirmation list); license_class keeps the stated license.
notes: Downloaded from a personal copy, dikal/maleo-emotion-annotated (DOI 10.57967/hf/10728, pinned revision); the original maleo-ai/maleo-emotion (DOI 10.57967/hf/6144) needs a Hugging Face login. The 700 audio files have the same Hugging Face LFS hashes as the original (project review). Labels are the main emotion; some examples have two overlapping emotions. The format is tied to the label: only the 40 neutral clips are compressed audio (20 MP3 and 20 AAC, all with a .WAV extension), and 20 happy clips are mono and 16 are 48 kHz (kept as they are, maintainer's decision). 4 clips are tagged [NO_SPEECH] (no human voice: disgust 2, fear 1, sad 1), used as they are; 27 are tagged [INAUDIBLE]. Speakers unknown. 700 clips, 0.59 h, converted to 16 kHz mono.

name: MASC
license_note: LDC license (terms for members and non-members).

name: MaSERC
full_title: MaSERC: A Dual-Scenario Marathi Emotional Speech Corpus for Speech Emotion Recognition Research
language_note: Marathi (dialect backgrounds such as Pune, Vidarbha, Marathwada, Konkan)
license_note: Mendeley Data license field: CC BY 4.0 (re-read through the Mendeley API, 2026-10-26; checked by the maintainer).
label_basis_note: Label = the emotion in the file name (the emotion the speaker was to deliver). The description reports a majority-vote validation by three annotators (kappa >= 0.78); their individual votes are not distributed.
notes: MaSERC (Marathi Speech Emotion Recognition Corpus), MIT Art, Design and Technology University, Pune; Mendeley Data b9jrrpdxgb version 1, 2026-06-22, one 285 MB zip. Native Marathi speakers (students and a few staff, aged 18-50, several dialect backgrounds), recorded in a partially controlled indoor room with a condenser microphone. Two scenarios (carrier sentence once per emotion; six-sentence exam monologue with one emotion per sentence). The description promises predefined splits, speaker metadata and scenario labels, but the release holds only 808 wav files. File names look like '<series> <number>[ name]-<Emotion>-<take>.wav' (the description gives another form); the emotion word is spelled in several ways (case, surpsise, Surprsie, suprise) and 11 names do not parse. 44.1 kHz stereo (42 files float), median 3.9 s, up to 12.3 s, 0.8214 h. 5 zero-length wav, 30 groups of byte-identical files (63 files), and 17 pairs of equal names holding different recordings. Speaker names appear in some file names and are not recorded here.

name: Montreal Affective Voices
full_title: The Montreal Affective Voices: A validated set of nonverbal affect bursts for research on auditory affective processing
license_note: Zenodo license field: CC BY 4.0 (re-read through the Zenodo API, 2026-10-26; checked by the maintainer). The record also holds the original paper as a PDF.
label_basis_note: Label = the emotion the actor was to portray (Sounds.csv Emotion; also in the file name). The paper's listening study (30 participants rated every vocalization; mean recognition accuracy 68%, highest 75% for women rating female voices) is not distributed per clip.
notes: Belin, Fillion-Bilodeau and Gosselin (Behavior Research Methods 40(2), 2008), deposited on Zenodo 2025-09-02 (3 files: Sounds.zip 7.6 MB, Sounds.csv, the paper PDF). 90 nonverbal affect bursts by 10 actors (5 male, 5 female) for 8 emotions plus neutral: anger, disgust, fear, pain, sadness, surprise, happiness, pleasure, neutral; 10 clips per label. 44.1 kHz mono 16-bit, 0.240-4.310 s, 0.0272 h. Sounds.csv holds F0 (min, max, median, SD), duration and power (median, SD) per clip; its Duration_ms column mixes units (41 rows in seconds, 49 in milliseconds). Ratings of valence, arousal and intensity by 30 participants are not distributed per clip.

name: MAVES DB
full_title: Malayalam Audio-Visual Emotional Speech Data
license_note: Mendeley Data licence field: CC BY 4.0, but only the data use agreement is deposited.

name: MCAE-SPPS
full_title: A validated Mandarin Chinese Auditory Emotion Database of Subject-Personal-Pronoun Sentences (MCAE-SPPS)
notes: MCAE-SPPS (OSF 9jyzc): only clips kept by the validation are distributed: 6,675 of 6 actors x 7 emotions x 200 sentences = 8,400. Clips per emotion are uneven (neutral 1,196 to fear 671). OSF publishes the MD5 of each zip. The evaluation tables give per-clip accuracy, vote breakdown, intensity (1-9), sentence and subject, acoustic values, rater group and rater information (not used by the recipe). A listening test with 720 raters exists (see human_accuracy_note).

name: MC-EIU
full_title: Emotion and Intent Joint Understanding in Multimodal Conversation: A Benchmarking Dataset
license_note: Hugging Face card: CC BY-NC 4.0. The scope of rights in the source TV dramas is not stated.
source_rights_note: Clips from 3 English and 4 Chinese TV series. The data license is CC BY-NC 4.0 (gated on Hugging Face); the rights in the series themselves were not found in the sources read. Needs a rights check; license_class keeps the stated license.
notes: Liu et al. (arXiv 2407.02751, 2024). 4,970 conversation clips from 3 English and 4 Chinese TV dramas. Split 7:1:2. Data of the ICASSP 2025 MEIJU challenge.

name: MDER-MA
full_title: MDER-MA: A multimodal dataset for emotion recognition in low-resource Moroccan Arabic language
source_rights_note: The clips are cut from Moroccan reality shows, radio, podcasts and interviews. The paper (Ethics Statement) says the data come from public sources, that the websites' terms of service were followed and that no consent was required; it names no sources and has no non-commercial statement. Needs a rights check (needs-confirmation list); license_class keeps the stated license.
notes: MDER-MA (Data in Brief 62 (2025) 112005): Moroccan Arabic (Darija) clips from reality shows, radio, podcasts and interviews. Release 1,345 WAV (paper: 1,322 samples, mono 16 kHz, about 3-20 s; measured: stereo 48 kHz, 1-51 s); 45 files without audio (44 bytes) and 33 content duplicates are removed, leaving 1,267 (2.11 h). The paper calls the UserID in the file name a number assigned per speaker (same speaker traceable across samples). 232 recordings are by speakers under 18. Only the 29 sad files use a different file-name form. 17 name collisions are different recordings, told apart by the SHA-256 prefix.

name: MELD
license_note: GitHub license of declare-lab/MELD: GPL-3.0 (re-read 2026-10-26; the DB records GPL-3.0-only). The material is clips of the TV series Friends, and the README states no rights for it. A footnote of the paper (ACL 2019) says the authors consulted a legal office to verify that use and distribution of very short videos fall under fair use (read and confirmed by the maintainer, 2026-10-26).
label_basis_note: Label = the majority of three annotators (graduate students) who judged each utterance with the video clip available (Section 3.1; Fleiss kappa 0.43). The original EmotionLines annotation had only the transcripts. The labels therefore are not judgements of the voice alone.
source_rights_note: Clips of the TV series Friends. The GPL-3.0 license in the repository covers the authors' work and the README states no rights for the material. A footnote of the paper (ACL 2019) says the authors consulted a legal office, which verified that use and distribution of very short videos fall under fair use. Marked cleared by the maintainer (2026-10-28); note that a fair-use opinion is not a license for commercial use.
notes: Audio is extracted from MP4 (mostly 6-channel AAC, converted to mono). Speakers are Friends character names (304, skewed to the six main characters). Has sentiment (positive/negative/neutral), Dialogue_ID, Season, Episode and timestamps. GitHub Issue #9 reports corrupted audio in about 200 training videos. The CSV files hold 13,708 utterances (train 9,989, valid 1,109, test 2,610); emotions: neutral 6,436, joy 2,308, surprise 1,636, anger 1,607, sadness 1,002, disgust 361, fear 358. The release has 2,060 macOS '._' stub files, one unreadable mp4, one CSV row without an mp4 and 141 mp4 without a CSV row. The four utterances left out are train Ross dia125 utt3 (corrupt mp4), valid Phoebe dia110 utt7 (no mp4), and test Student dia38 utt4 (305 s) and Phoebe dia220 utt0 (235 s), whose CSV intervals cover minutes of audio under one label. Groups of identical sound (from the review, not recomputed here): 43 groups and 91 clips, 24 of them with different emotions in the group (for example four utterances of one test dialogue labelled neutral, happy, angry and angry), probably neighbouring cuts with overlapping subtitle times (a guess), and 3 spanning the official train and test splits (train dia12 utt7 and 8 with test dia85 utt0 and 1; train dia887 utt0 with test dia117 utt8).

name: MEmoR
full_title: MEmoR: A Dataset for Multimodal Emotion Reasoning in Videos
license_note: Use requires signing a License Agreement (content not checked).
labels_discrete_note: Basic emotions and 14 fine-grained emotions (list not checked)
notes: Shen et al. (Tsinghua University, ACM MM 2020). Emotions are annotated for non-speaking characters as well as speakers, together with personality traits.

name: MER2023
labels_discrete_note: multiple emotion categories; verify exact label vocabulary in the released annotation file
source_rights_note: Video clips from films and TV series. The challenge EULA restricts use; nothing read about the rights in the source material. Needs a rights check; license_class keeps the stated license.
notes: The 5,030 labelled clips of MER2023 are used unchanged as Train&Val of MER2024, and C²SER and others call the same 5,030 clips (5.9 hours) "MER2024". The unlabelled part of MER2023 has 73,982 clips.

name: MER2024
full_title: MER 2024: Semi-Supervised Learning, Noise Robustness, and Open-Vocabulary Multimodal Emotion Recognition
license_note: The Hugging Face card says academic use only, an EULA must be accepted, and redistribution and modification are prohibited. The gate text limits use to academic research with the permission of the Intelligent Interaction Group. Hugging Face license tag: cc-by-nc-4.0.
labels_discrete_note: MER-OV (322 clips; the text says 332, disagreeing with the table) has open-vocabulary labels.
notes: Lian et al. (MRAC workshop at ACM MM 2024). The 5,030 Train&Val clips are all the labelled clips of MER2023 (§2). MER-SEMI and MER-NOISE each have about 1,170 clips chosen from 115,595 unlabelled clips where at least 4 of 5 annotators agreed. MER-NOISE adds noise to the audio and blurs the video. The Hugging Face release has video, subtitles (Chinese and English), discrete labels, EMER descriptions (332 clips) and open-vocabulary labels.

name: MER2025
labels_discrete_note: worried, happy, neutral, angry, surprise, sad; fine-grained open-vocabulary emotions
notes: Paper arXiv 2504.19423 (ACM MM 2025): the EULA allows academic research only, forbids modification and re-uploading, and strictly forbids human annotation of MER2025 samples. The Hugging Face release also contains training CSVs for MER-Caption, MER-Caption+ and OV-MERD (track2/track3). Hugging Face gated value: auto (2026-10-23).

name: MER2026
labels_discrete_note: interlocutor emotions; fine-grained open-vocabulary emotions

name: MER-Caption / MER-Caption+
full_title: MER-Caption, MER-Caption+ (description data of AffectGPT)
license_note: The paper says it is limited to CC BY-NC 4.0. Audio and video follow the MER2024 EULA.
notes: Lian et al. (ICML 2025, AffectGPT). MER-Caption: 115,595 items (2,932 distinct labels); the filtered MER-Caption+: 31,327 items (1,972 labels). Included in MERChallenge/MER2025 on Hugging Face as training CSVs for track2/track3.

name: MERR
full_title: MERR: Multimodal Emotion Recognition and Reasoning dataset(Emotion-LLaMA)
license_note: The data follows the MER2023 EULA (academic research only). Code: BSD-3-Clause.
notes: Cheng et al. (NeurIPS 2024, Emotion-LLaMA). From over 70,000 unlabelled MER2023 segments, 28,618 coarse annotations were made by combining facial Action Units, audio cues from Qwen-Audio and integration by LLaMA-3; 4,487 fine-grained annotations confirmed by a vote of 4 experts were selected.

name: MESD
full_title: Mexican Emotional Speech Database (MESD)
notes: The release also contains 288 processed (naturalness-reduced) items; human recordings are 862. The difference from the paper's 864 cannot be checked in the release (one child recording each is missing for Anger and Neutral, leaving 143). Single-word utterances. Mendeley rejects the default User-Agent with 403. Per voice type (female, male, child) each emotion is spoken by fixed speakers, so the voice reveals the emotion (recorded only; the data is used as it is, maintainer's decision). The release holds 3 women, 2 men and 6 children; the paper says 8 adults and 8 children. Single-word utterances. One same-sound pair (Happiness_C_A_dentro and Happiness_C_A_lento_dentro, different word names): exclude_duplicates (default false) drops the later one. Corpus A shares 24 words; corpus B has 24 different words per emotion.

name: MES-P
full_title: MES-P: An Emotional Tonal Speech Dataset in Mandarin with Distal and Proximal Labels
labels_discrete_note: Two kinds of labels: intended emotion (distal) and perceived emotion (proximal). Joy, anger and sadness at two levels, moderate and strong
notes: Xiao et al. (Soochow University, built 2017, IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing 2019). 16 native speakers (8 male, 8 female) acted 16 phoneme-balanced sentences: 5,376 utterances. The tone distribution was matched to spoken language.

name: MESS
full_title: Morgan Emotional Speech Set (MESS)
labels_discrete_note: categorical emotion ratings available from the researcher
notes: Morgan (2019, J. Speech Lang. Hear. Res. 62(11):4015-4029). Zenodo 3813437 and 7378320. 6 people (3 male, 3 female) recorded in 4 speaking styles. Stimulus sentences substitute words into 3 frames. Listener ratings are available on request from the researcher; the recipe uses only the intended-acting labels in the file names. The mapping from the first letter of the file name to the emotion name is inferred, not documented. Six drama students (University of Utah, 19-21 years) recorded sentences in a sound-treated room (Shure SM10 head-mounted microphone). For each cue name x emotion x talker, five of the recorded sentences were removed: errors first, otherwise the tokens least representative of their emotion category (largest distance from the category's mean ratings). Calm replaces neutral because neutral carries negative valence (authors). Men and women read the same set of sentence frames; within a gender each speaker has different sentences. A listening test with 10 listeners covers all 2,160 recordings (see human_accuracy_note).

name: MIKU-EmoBench
language_note: Neither the paper nor the card states the language; they only mention regional diversity (US, Europe, Asia). mul follows "Multiple" in Table I of the MSP-Podcast paper
license_note: CC BY 3.0 is the license of the annotation files on Hugging Face. The audio is not distributed.
labels_discrete_note: 26 categories: Cowen et al.'s 27 minus one removed for ethical reasons. Each utterance has proportions of several emotions (e.g. Interest:60%, Confusion:30%) and a confidence
notes: Cheng, Zhang, Shi (arXiv 2505.15772, 2025). Collected automatically from YouTube with MIKU-PAL (face detection, speaker identification, MLLM). Built as a benchmark for emotional TTS. The paper gives 65,970 utterances and 131.2 hours; the card gives 89,428 utterances and about 160 hours (updated after the paper was submitted).

name: MInDS-14
full_title: MInDS-14: Multilingual Intent Detection from Speech
language_note: English in three varieties (UK, US, Australia). 14 languages and locales in total.

name: MLEnd Spoken Numerals
language_note: English numerals. Speakers from 31 nationalities and 42 language backgrounds
license_note: Kaggle license field: Unknown (same through the authenticated API).
labels_discrete_note: Measured Intonation column (32,654 rows): excited 8223, question 8202, neutral 8187, bored 8042.
notes: Made by students of Queen Mary University of London (Kaggle creator Jesus Requena). Over 32,000 recordings by 154 people. With demographic information. The same series includes MLEnd Hums and Whistles.

name: M-MELD
full_title: M-MELD: A Multilingual Multi-Party Dataset for Emotion Recognition in Conversations
language_note: Greek, Polish, French, Spanish (translations of MELD's English utterances)
notes: Ghosh et al. (arXiv 2203.16799, 2022). Human translations made from foreign-language subtitles, not machine translation.

name: MSP-Face
full_title: MSP-Face corpus: A natural audiovisual emotional database
language_note: The page does not state the language (monologues from a video-sharing site)
license_note: Shared as an Academic License (page text). The terms document was not read.
notes: Vidal, Salman, Lin, Busso (ICMI 2020), UT Dallas MSP Lab. Natural videos of people talking to the camera about everyday events and opinions. 9,370 labelled clips (24 h 41 min) and 15,011 unlabelled (38 h 3 min).

name: MSP-IMPROV
labels_discrete_note: anger, happiness, sadness, neutral, other/no agreement

name: MSP-Podcast
license_note: Signed agreement with the MSP lab (University of Texas at Dallas): internal non-commercial research only, no redistribution, and citation of Lotfian & Busso (2019) is required. The maintainer confirmed the terms are acceptable (2026-10-26). On the requires-application list.
notes: Release 2.0; the recipe does not download (Audios/ and Labels/labels_consensus.csv come from the lab). Paper arXiv 2509.09791v1: 1,446,270 annotations by 13,280 annotators. Primary-emotion agreement 0.411, called Cohen's kappa in the title of Table III and Fleiss' kappa in section VI (inconsistent within the paper). Byte-identical audio: 2,760 groups, 8,180 files; whether their labels agree is not checked and they are used as they are (maintainer's decision: on hold, noted only). Class counts in train: neutral 51,151, happy 37,048, angry 22,609, sad 18,256, surprise 3,220, contempt 2,765, disgust 1,325, fear 794. naturalvoices extends the same source podcast recordings to all speaker turns (5,049 hours; arXiv 2511.00256).

name: MultiDialog
full_title: Let's Go Real Talk: Spoken Dialogue Model for Face-to-Face Conversation (MultiDialog dataset)
license_note: The Hugging Face card's license says only cc, without the CC type or version.
labels_discrete_note: Per utterance the metadata has 8 values: Neutral, Happy, Fear, Angry, Disgusting, Surprising, Sad and Curious to dive deeper (43%). The paper says Neutral and Curious to dive deeper were recorded as one label (no visible difference), giving 7. The recipe merges curious into neutral (switch merge_labels). Dialogues by actors whose emotion-acting accuracy exceeded 40% (a, b, c, e, f, g, i, j, k) form the gold emotion subset: 143,816 files / 245.4 h by file name (last character = actor); the other actors (d, h, l) have 43,917 files / 79.6 h.
label_basis_note: The label is the emotion shown to the actor with the script line. The 25-person user study checked a sample of 70 utterances.
source_rights_note: Recordings are the authors' own; the dialogue scripts are taken from Topical-Chat, and their license was not checked.
notes: Park et al. (KAIST, ACL 2024). Face-to-face conversations based on TopicalChat scripts. 8,733 dialogues, 187,859 utterances, 339.71 hours; splits train, valid_freq, valid_rare, test_freq, test_rare. The speaker ID is the last character of the file name. Measured: 187,854 files, 325.45 h, 16 kHz mono; one pair with the same sound under conflicting labels (not used). Download 33 GB, extracted about 36 GB.

name: Narrative Dialogue Dataset
license_note: The Zenodo record and the paper's Data availability say CC BY 4.0.
notes: 2,588 short stories, 27,074 utterances, 2,582 characters. 6 emotions (Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear, Disgust, Surprise). Based on honicky/short_childrens_stories_with_labeled_character_names on Hugging Face.

name: NaturalVoices
full_title: NaturalVoices: A Large-Scale, Spontaneous and Emotional Podcast Dataset for Voice Conversion
license_note: The NaturalVoices_EVC card on Hugging Face states no license.
notes: Du et al., Busso (JHU and the MSP Lab at CMU, arXiv 2511.00256, 2025). 5,049 hours, 6,790 episodes in total. Hugging Face has 870 hours for VC, a 10% subset, and an emotion-balanced EVC set (about 370 hours). The full set and the collection pipeline are on GitHub (Lab-MSP/NaturalVoices). Paper: over 6,790 Creative Commons-licensed episodes, over 2,670 speakers (Table I). Built on the same source podcast recordings as MSP-Podcast, extending the human-annotated part of MSP-Podcast (409 hours) to all speaker turns.

name: nEMO
full_title: nEMO: Dataset of Emotional Speech in Polish
notes: Distributed as parquet on Hugging Face (audio bytes embedded in the table). The card states it is "provided without splits". 5 male and 4 female speakers, 256-540 clips each. Home recordings, so equipment and rooms probably differ by speaker. Speakers differ in class counts (MK0 has no surprise; MP0 has 256 clips). 9 speakers: 3 qualified voice actors and 6 non-professional.

name: Nexdata 20 People English Emotional Speech Data
license_note: The README says Commercial License.
notes: 20 Americans (half female) each read 2,100 sentences of 10 kinds of emotional text. 44.1 kHz 16-bit.

name: NonverbalTTS
full_title: NonverbalTTS: A Public English Corpus of Text-Aligned Nonverbal Vocalizations with Emotion Annotations for Text-to-Speech
license_note: Hugging Face card text: annotations under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; audio under the licenses of the sources (VoxCeleb, Expresso). The Hugging Face metadata field says apache-2.0, which disagrees with the text and is not adopted (maintainer's decision). Expresso is CC BY-NC 4.0 (https://speechbot.github.io/expresso/). VoxCeleb's vox1 page at VGG gives CC BY-SA 4.0 for the "metadata" (nothing about the audio itself). Evaluation use only.
labels_discrete_note: One emotion per clip: emotion2vec+ large's automatic classification reviewed by 3 annotators (paper §3.2, §3.3). Details of human involvement and label reliability unverified. Overall: neutral 2,406 / happy 1,605 / other 1,177 / sad 387 / disgusted 78 / surprised 34 / angry 25 / fearful 10 / untagged 534 (matches paper Table 6; untagged means annotators disagreed, about 8.5% per paper §4.2). other is an ambiguous category outside the 8 emotions (paper §4.2).
label_basis_note: Audio cut from VoxCeleb (natural speech such as interviews) and Expresso (actors' read and improvised performances). Emotions were classified automatically into 8 classes by emotion2vec+ large; annotators listened and replaced them where needed (Argilla; annotators were given definitions of each emotion). The number of raters and how judgements were combined are not described. Expresso's style tags are not used.
notes: Borisov et al. (SSW 2025), deepvk. 17 hours, 2,296 speakers. Hugging Face splits: train 3,641, dev 46, test 359, other 2,210 (6,256 rows in total). The paper's splits are only train/dev/test (Table 5; the paper's train is 3,642, one more than measured). The public split other (2,210 clips) is not explained by the paper or card and is not used in the official experiments. It carries emotion and other annotations, but the recipe does not use it. Measured: 1,373 of the 1,378 clips without NVs and 522 of the 534 untagged clips are in other, and the share with transcripts from all 3 annotators is low (47%, vs 75-84% in the other splits). The public split other and the emotion label other are different things. Audio: 4,452 clips from VoxCeleb (13.68 h, 16 kHz) and 1,804 from Expresso (3.91 h, 48 kHz), distinguishable by the data_name column. The train and test counts of paper Table 7 (emotions per split) do not match the measurements. Of the 6,256 clips (17.59 h), the recipe uses 3,201 (8.12 h), excluding the public split other (2,210), emotion other (833) and untagged (12); NVs are not used because a clip can contain several (multi-label). Position (maintainer's decision): evaluation only. The VoxCeleb part is in-the-wild YouTube audio, an evaluation set close to YODAS, worth looking at separately. The Expresso part is read and improvised dialogue of a different nature. Emotion labels are automatic classification plus annotator review; their reliability needs checking.

Same recording with different labels: m/sessc/30a07Ca.wav (speaker 30, sentence 07, angry) and m/sesst/41a11Ta.wav (speaker 41, sentence 11, sad) have identical samples in both channels; 41a11Ta looks like the copy and exclude_duplicates (default false) drops it. The two channels come from different microphones and are partly uncorrelated, so only the left channel is used. Distributed as RAR; extraction needs bsdtar.

full_title: PAVOQUE
labels_discrete_note: cheerful/optimistic, gloomy/pessimistic, aggressive/confrontational, cool/laid-back, neutral
notes: 5 FLAC files and 5 YAML files from GitHub Releases v0.2. The difference between the spreadsheet's 7,334 utterances / 12.2 hours and the recipe's 5,442 / 8.6 hours is unexplained (pavoque-outtakes, 319 MB, is not used because its content is unverified). poker is a calm speaking style outside the common 7. neutral is 57%, a strong skew. Utterances include trailing silence; no trimming. Measured per style: the median share of power below 40 Hz is 0.02-0.14 and the 90th percentile 0.07-0.47, so correlations of unfiltered waveforms are high even across different utterances. poker is a cool gambler's speaking style specific to this corpus. The spreadsheet's 7,334 clips / 12.2 h versus the real 5,442 / 8.6 h is unexplained.

name: Rasa
full_title: Rasa: Building Expressive Speech Synthesis Systems for Indian Languages in Low-resource Settings
language_note: 22 scheduled languages of India. The paper covers Assamese, Bengali and Tamil; the card tags list 13 codes; the repository folders hold all 22.
license_note: Hugging Face card: CC-BY-4.0 (gated: auto). An aggregator listing (AIKosh) gives CC BY-ND 4.0, which disagrees.
labels_discrete_note: Emotion styles: happy, anger, fear, surprise, disgust, sad. Eleven further styles are text types: wiki, conv, proper_noun, book, news, alexa, indic, bb, umang, digi, sangrah. The label is the style (the kind of text the voice artist read), assigned at recording.
label_basis_note: Intended: the style assigned to the text read. The paper's human checks are on the English emotion sentences (does the text convey the emotion) and on synthesised speech (MUSHRA, 22 listeners), not on these recordings.
source_rights_note: Voice artists recorded for the dataset with signed consent, payment and ethics approval (described for 3 languages in the paper; the other 19 are not described; the maintainer trusts the authors' license).
notes: Srinivasa Varadhan, Sankar, Raju, Khapra (AI4Bharat, Interspeech 2024). At the time of the paper: 10 hours of neutral and 1-3 hours per emotion for each language. Kaggle has a derivative of the Punjabi part (fatimatuzahra9115, 9,634 clips). WHOLE-CORPUS FIGURES (not emotion data): 640,946 utterances, 1,145.4 h in the converted files; the six emotion styles are 124,842 utterances and 280.4 h, and the other 11 styles (Wikipedia, conversation, news, books, proper nouns, voice commands) are 516,104 utterances and 865.0 h, about 80% of utterances. They are not emotion recognition data. 1,317 parquet files, 22 languages. 70 file names collide (Tamil male TAM_M_NAMES_*): the same audio carries different DIGI and PROPER NOUN texts (TAM_M_NAMES_00106 was listened to: the proper-noun text is right); the recipe drops both. 2,529 byte-identical pairs (same speaker and style, 464 across the official train and test) of which the recipe keeps one by default. SANGRAH is Bengali male only (1,837), INDIC has 12 languages. One empty wav (ASM_F_INDIC_00001).

name: ReCANVo
full_title: ReCANVo: A Database of Real-World Communicative and Affective Nonverbal Vocalizations
license_note: Zenodo license field: CC BY 3.0 US. The Zenodo description asks for the paper Johnson & Narain et al. (Sci Data 10, 523, 2023, doi 10.1038/s41597-023-02405-7) to be cited.
labels_discrete_note: 6 labels shared by all participants (delighted, dysregulated, frustrated, request, self-talk, social) and up to 4 individual labels chosen by the family from 25 options (paper, Methods). Labels were assigned on the spot by family members (one label per vocalisation). The CSV has 22 kinds (self-talk written `selftalk`): selftalk 1885, frustrated 1536, delighted 1272, dysregulated 704, social 634, request 419, affectionate 129, yes 123, laughter 93, dysregulation-sick 74, happy 61, help 24, more 22, protest 21, bathroom 20, dysregulation-bathroom 18, no 12, glee 8, laugh 8, tablet 7, hunger 4, greeting 3. Paper Table 2 has 21 kinds, without `laugh` (8 clips, all P03). Participant x label counts match Table 2 except one cell: P03 laughter (8) in Table 2, while the CSV has 0 `laughter` and 8 `laugh` for P03. Following the paper, they are treated as the same label (maintainer's decision).
label_basis_note: Non-verbal vocalisations produced in daily life (home, school, etc.) by people with very little spoken language. Labels were assigned on the spot by a parent or caregiver who knew the person well (real time, one person, judging with full view of the situation). Labels include intents such as requests as well as emotions.
notes: Johnson & Narain et al. (MIT Media Lab, Scientific Data 2023). 8 participants (paper Tables 1 and 2: 6 male, 2 female), aged 6-23, with diagnoses of autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy or genetic conditions. Wearable recordings at home and school. The paper calls people with about 0-10 spoken words minimally speaking (the Zenodo description says non-speaking). Measured: 7,077 clips, 2.461 h, 0.082-14.057 s (median 0.949 s). The Zenodo description says "approximately 0.5-4 seconds", but 1,043 clips are under 0.5 s and 169 over 4 s. Audio is 44.1 kHz (the paper says 16-bit), mixed: 4,281 mono, 2,796 stereo; 5,466 PCM_16, 1,611 PCM_32. Clips per participant: P01 1,708 / P08 1,545 / P05 1,028 / P16 779 / P06 569 / P02 557 / P03 525 / P11 366. The bundled `Communication_Profiles.xlsx` (participant questionnaire, not clip labels) covers only 7 people and lacks P02 (the paper says a separate .csv, but the release has .xlsx). File names follow the paper's format, with 38 exceptions. Of the 7,077 clips, the recipe uses 7,051, excluding 26 train/valid clips under 0.2 s (WavLM's SpecAugment fails under 0.205 s; the maintainer listened to the 29 clips under 0.2 s and agreed to exclude them). Position: everyday non-verbal sounds of people with little speech; labels are a mix of emotions and communicative intents assigned by family members. Whether speaker-specific voices confuse training is unverified. Inclusion in multi-corpus training is undecided (idea: include it, and if time allows compare with a version without it).

name: RESD
full_title: Russian Emotional Speech Dialogs (RESD)
notes: Official split exists (train 1116 / test 280). Includes its own label, enthusiasm. Sample rates 16 kHz and 44.1 kHz are mixed. Individual speakers cannot be identified from file names. Dialogue corpus: 20 voice actors in pairs improvised 50 dialogues (unscripted words; emotions assigned in secret beforehand). The file name <dialogue>_<emotion1>_<emotion2>_<role>_<turn> carries the dialogue number, the two partners' emotions, the role letter of the speaker and the turn number; in all 1,396 files the role letter matches the label. Sample rate is constant within a dialogue (16 kHz 716 clips, 44.1 kHz 680 clips). Context-aware analysis is possible; a context column was not added to the schema, so the context items are listed in annotations.

release_version: Kaggle version 1 (Initial release), last updated 2021-06-09, one zip (4,513,296,896 bytes)
labels_discrete_note: Labels are only the emotion codes in file names (an / di / fe / ha / sa / su), 120 each, 720 in total. The per-file emotion is the instruction to the performer; the Kaggle description says only samples for which all of at least two listeners who did not know the language perceived the intended emotion were taken for experiments (about 500 samples). Neither the test results nor a mark of which ~500 files are in the release. The recipe uses 714 clips after removing 6 with identical md5.
label_basis_note: Video recordings of 8 people expressing 6 emotions in 6 languages. Labels are the intended emotions. A listening test kept only clips where all of at least two raters who did not know the language perceived the intended emotion (whether they watched the video is not stated).
notes: Ryerson Multimedia Lab (Wang & Guan, IEEE Trans. Multimedia 2008, etc.). 8 subjects, 6 languages (Kaggle description: English, Mandarin, Urdu, Punjabi, Persian, Italian). The description's audio specification is 22,050 Hz, single channel, 16-bit, video 30 fps, but the actual files are PCM 16-bit stereo inside avi, 669 at 44.1 kHz and 51 at 48 kHz (the two channels differ in all 720). 2.13-8.37 s (mean 4.94 s), 0.987 h in total. The release has 720 avi files, which does not match the description's "about 500 samples". 5 groups (11 clips) have identical md5 (within the same subject, folder and emotion; the maintainer listened and confirmed the audio is the same utterance; the recipe keeps only the lowest-numbered one and excludes the other 6). The release has no label files other than the emotion codes in file names, no transcripts and no listening-test results. An acted audio-visual database. Only 8 subjects, and the split is by subject folder, so the emotion make-up of each split is skewed (e.g. valid has 8 angry and 18 happy). Since the license is Unknown, how to use it (evaluation only, etc.) awaits the team's confirmation.

label_basis_note: MBROLA diphone synthesis with rule-based prosody manipulation for 3 emotions and neutral. Labels are the synthesis target emotion. When the rules were set, a forced-choice listening experiment with 20 participants gave a mean accuracy of 0.5 (not a per-clip selection).
notes: Burkhardt, Eyben, Schuller (LREC 2022 DCLRL workshop). Synthetic data (not human speech): MBROLA diphone synthesis with emotion-like prosody applied by Emofilt rules. The release has 6,001 wav files (the paper says 6,000; reads as a one-off from the generation script's stop condition, but that is a guess). 16 kHz mono 16-bit, 0.819-30.506 s, 11.1437 h in total, 6 voices. Cause unverified (hypothesis: the generation script reuses a temporary file and does not check for failure). The paper's listening test (20 people, forced choice) gives neutral .6, happiness .35, sadness .5, anger .55 (mean .5): hard for people to tell apart. Voice genders disagree between sources (paper and `db.yaml` vs the GitHub script), so none are given. The Zenodo description says "three basic emotions", but the paper and release have 5 + neutral, 6 classes. The maintainer's assessment: quite poor synthetic data; unsure whether to use it in experiments (2026-10-20).

Possible label errors: the 3 clips `S95_BIL_CO14_G3` in the neutral folder (`d01_v1`, `d01_v2`, `d03_v1`; speaker SPKM03) sounded angry to the maintainer (2026-10-20), and their median F0 (176-179 Hz) is closer to that speaker's angry (192-229 Hz) than neutral (133-139 Hz) (their loudness is lower, not matching angry). With no documentation this cannot be settled, so the label stays neutral as distributed (maintainer's decision). Only part was listened to, so other errors may exist.

Agreement (the share of votes on the majority emotion) is stored per recording in the data; the paper recommends removing agreement below 0.71 (alpha 0.692, the smallest threshold that gives alpha at least 0.667); in version 2.0 this keeps 14,181 recordings (14,182 in version 1). Not used: 2,664 recordings with no majority (None) and 5 'other', and the studio clip and middle microphone channels. Of the 25,185 used, 16,491 (65%) have a majority equal to the instruction; for agreement of at least 0.71 it is 10,942 of 14,181 (77%) and below it 5,549 of 11,004 (50%). Share kept at 0.71 per emotion: frustrated 44%, neutral 57%, sad 57%, angry 63%, happy 73%. Three byte-identical pairs (same label): s001_con_actor002_impro1_25/_28, s048_con_actor136_impro6_9/_10, s078_con_actor195_impro12_7/_8. The longest recording is 108.8 s. No checksums published.

USC-EMO-MRI: An emotional speech production database [Dataset]. 10th International Seminar on Speech Production (ISSP). USC-EMO-MRI corpus: An emotional speech production database recorded by real-time magnetic resonance imaging, Cologne, Germany. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19325044. The CSL paper (doi 10.1016/j.csl.2020.101100) is related but is not the citation for this corpus.
release_version: The single version of Zenodo 19325044 (created 2026-03-30, publication_date 2014-05-08). zip md5 65fa5b0cf0337a873227a490d56fdaf3
labels_discrete_note: `emotion ID` in `labels/meta` (README: the final label determined by listener evaluation). 1 neutral 656 / 2 angry 563 / 3 happy 542 / 4 sad 544 / 5: 29 (an ID the README does not explain; the paper's evaluation options include "other", but no source says 5 is other). 29 utterances have no row in `meta` and no label (the timing table has 2,363 rows, `meta` 2,334). The recipe uses the 2,305 utterances with IDs 1-4.
label_basis_note: 10 professional actors portrayed 4 target emotions. Each utterance was rated by at least 10 raters (professional actors) from the audio only: the best emotion of 5 choices (neutral, anger, happiness, sadness, other), confidence, and strength of expression (5 levels). The final label is the majority vote; ties go to the higher mean confidence. The recipe uses this final evaluation label (emotion ID in meta), not the target emotion.
notes: Kim, Toutios, Lee, Narayanan (USC SAIL). 5 men and 5 women with professional acting experience lay supine in an MRI scanner and read English sentences (6 sentences + repeated utterances for some speakers + the Grandfather passage) in 4 target emotions. The MRI captures the mid-sagittal plane of the vocal tract at 23.18 frames/s and 68x68 pixels; audio was recorded simultaneously at 20 kHz and denoised afterwards with adaptive signal processing (paper §2.2). Fast speaking rate only for neutral (98 utterances). The archive is AVI (video + audio); there are no wav files. Labels are the majority vote of the emotion perceived by 10-12 listeners (paper §2.3; listeners per speaker in Table 2); agreement with the target emotion ranges from 69.5% (M2) to 94.0% (F2) as speaker means. Per-rater choices, confidence and strength, and the performers' target emotions, are not in the archive (the paper's Data availability says "the emotion evaluation result of each utterance" is public). 26 AVI files (including 3 in `f3/avi/palate_sweep/`) do not appear in the timing table and are not explained in the README. Measured: 10 speakers, 356 AVI files, 2,363 utterances in the timing table, 2,334 with labels (2,305 with IDs 1-4). Speech acted inside an MRI scanner, not a corpus built for speech emotion recognition (the paper studies the articulation of emotional expression). The remaining noise level was not measured. Labels are the listeners' majority vote and some differ from the performers' intention. The recipe's valid set is a single speaker (f2). How to use it in multi-corpus training is undecided.

The copy used has one parquet (373 MB) with columns speaker_id, path (audio), duration, accent, emotion, emotion_id and gender. 5,280 rows, 3.176 h; neutral 1,507, angry 1,466, happy 1,228, sad 1,079; accents south 3,618, north 1,336, mid 326; gender female 3,675, male 1,605. name: VIVAE
full_title: The Variably Intense Vocalizations of Affect and Emotion Corpus (VIVAE)
source_rights_note: Recorded by the authors (non-professional actresses at Berklee College of Music, Boston).
notes: Holz, Larrouy-Maestri, Poeppel (2022, Emotion 22(1):213-225). VIVAE.zip from Zenodo 4066235; MD5 matches. Only the full_set (1,085 clips) is used (core_set, 480, is a subset). Intensity: low 262 / moderate 269 / strong 282 / peak 272. 120 clips are shorter than 0.5 s. Corpus paper: Emotion 22(1):213-225 (doi 10.1037/emo0001048); the rating experiments are in the companion Sci Rep 11:9663 (2021). The earlier paper_url pointed to an unrelated article and was replaced. The core set (480 clips = 6 emotions x 4 intensities x 10 speakers x 2) contains S01-S10 only (48 each); S11 (54 clips) is in the full set only. The core_set folder of the zip allows selecting it later by file name; the recipe stores no core flag. Core-set speakers are described as 10 non-professional actresses; S11 is not described in the sources read. The number of raters per clip and the selection threshold were not found. Overall accuracy is described only as lower than in earlier studies (per emotion in the paper's figures and supplementary table S2).

Majestrino and Multilingual In The Wild are speech corpora without emotion labels whose only emotion-related attributes are these automatic annotations, so they are not rows.

name: WHiSER
full_title: WHiSER: White House Tapes Speech Emotion Recognition Corpus
language_note: The paper does not state the language. Conversations in President Nixon's office (1971-1973)
license_note: The GitHub repository (msplabresearch/WHiSER, commit 5850655514dd, 2024-09-03) has no license file; the README and the paper state no terms of use. The audio is derived from recordings published by the Nixon Presidential Library. The maintainer will ask the authors (MSP lab) about license and citation (2026-10-26; not yet contacted); until then it is used locally only and not redistributed.
labels_discrete_note: Consensus is by plurality. X (no agreement) and O (other) also exist. Distributed labels: N 3,492, X 916, H 345, A 293, S 284, O 47, U 33, C 10, F 6, D 1
label_basis_note: Label = the plurality of at least five student workers' choices among eight primary emotions (A anger, C contempt, D disgust, F fear, H happy, N neutral, S sad, U surprise; O other and X no agreement are also coded). Individual annotations (with worker ids) and secondary emotions are in labels_detailed.csv. The 5,427 clips were first selected by emotion recognition models trained on MSP-Podcast (including a manual removal of unintelligible clips) so that they are likely to be emotional.
notes: Naini, Goncalves, Kohler, Robinson, Richerson and Busso (MSP lab, Interspeech 2024, pp. 1595-1599). Natural emotional speech from the Nixon White House tapes (1971-1973; Oval Office, Cabinet Room, telephone and other places) selected and annotated with the AndC pipeline: audio was converted to 16 kHz 16-bit mono, voice-activity segmented, filtered for music and noise (5 dB SNR floor), and emotionally likely turns were retrieved with models trained on MSP-Podcast; unintelligible ones were removed by hand. 5,427 clips of 3-11 s are annotated by 33 student workers, at least five per turn, with a primary emotion (8 options plus other), secondary emotions (16 kinds), and arousal, valence and dominance on a 7-point scale. The distributed wav files are 44.1 kHz (5,255) or 22.05 kHz (172) mono 32-bit float, 3.010-10.990 s, 6.3548 h (the paper says 16 kHz 16-bit and 6 h 21 min). Primary labels in labels_consensus.csv: N 3,492; X 916; H 345; A 293; S 284; O 47; U 33; C 10; F 6; D 1. SpkrID is Unknown and Split_Set NA for every file. The README lists Annotation_wav_files_ref.txt (mapping to the source recordings), which is not published. The paper says duplicates were removed, but 53 groups (107 clips) of the same sound remain, most of them the same tape under another name (e.g. rmn_e655a and rmn_e655b), 22 of them across the recipe's splits before exclusion.

Counts in the paper's Table 1 (angry 268, happy 249, sad 303, fear 244, neutral 305; 1,369) differ from the release (angry 286, happy 294, sad 303, fear 244, neutral 305; 1,432).
